title: Member of Security Staff, Privacy & Trust Ops Lead
description:
About Arena Intelligence

Arena is the platform for evaluating how AI models perform in the real world. Founded by researchers from UC Berkeley's SkyLab, we're on a mission to measure and advance the frontier of AI for real-world use, and to build the foundation for everyone to understand, shape, and benefit from it.


Tens of millions of people use Arena each month to evaluate how frontier systems handle the work they actually do. The preferences they share power the most transparent, rigorous, and human-centered evaluations in AI. Leading AI labs, enterprises, and independent researchers rely on our work and open datasets to understand how models behave in real workflows: agentic coding, creative generation, professional productivity, and beyond. We go beyond leaderboards and decompose what human experience reveals about AI, so models advance toward the work people actually do.


We're a team of researchers, academics, builders, and creatives from UC Berkeley, Google, Stanford, and DeepMind. We seek truth, move fast, and value craftsmanship, curiosity, and impact over hierarchy. We're building a company where thoughtful, curious people from all backgrounds can do their best work together, in an office culture that radiates excellence, energy, and focus.

We're hiring the first dedicated owner of privacy, compliance, and trust operations at Arena. This is a build-from-here role. You'll be hands-on from day one, maturing core parts of the program as you go, and you'll decide what to prioritize first.

You'll partner closely with Engineering, driving privacy and trust engineering initiatives, like de-identification, pseudonymous identifiers, and data lifecycle controls, from requirements through to what actually ships in the product.

You'll also work closely with our Legal Team, who own the legal determinations. You own the operations underneath them: the programs that make those decisions real, evidenced, and repeatable.

This role is onsite in our San Francisco office. It works directly with our leadership team, and being in the room is part of the job.

What You'll Own

Privacy operations and the commercial data path. The privacy program end-to-end: records of processing, data subject rights, retention, breach notification, and the privacy notices that face millions of users. This also covers the compliance work behind how Arena's data products are packaged and shared externally.

Compliance, risk, and third-party management. The control framework portfolio (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, NIST AI RMF), our continuous compliance monitoring program, and a risk register with accountable business owners. You'll also own third-party risk management end-to-end, and privacy for the API and gateway, including the sub-processor register behind our enterprise customer terms.

Model-provider compliance. Arena's relationships with frontier labs are each their own compliance surface: data processing terms, acceptable-use obligations, provider provenance and screening, and trust operations when something escalates in either direction. This barely exists as a named job anywhere else.

Trust and safety governance. Mandated reporting and the clocks attached to it, evidence preservation, oversight of whether moderation actually works, and the enforcement policy underneath it.

The Authority That Comes With It

  • A gate on vendor and provider onboarding: your review has to close before onboarding proceeds

  • A named escalation path to the Executive Team when a proposed risk treatment is refused

  • A voice in major product and commercial decisions that touch trust, privacy, or data

  • Sign-off on compliance representations: nothing goes to a customer, provider, auditor, or regulator claiming a control we don't have

You'll Have

  • A track record of building a privacy or compliance program somewhere it didn't exist

  • Enough technical fluency to work directly with engineers on privacy and trust systems, reading a schema, reasoning about a data flow, and driving initiatives like de-identification and data lifecycle controls from requirements through to what ships

  • Real depth in GDPR and US state privacy regimes: you can run a DPIA yourself and reason about controller/processor boundaries in a genuinely ambiguous relationship

  • Audit experience from the inside: SOC 2 and ideally ISO 27001, owning evidence and control narratives rather than coordinating someone else who did

  • Experience owning an external party relationship where the obligations were contractual and the follow-through was on you

  • Experience on the commercial side of privacy, where the program gates revenue, not just protects data

  • An obligation you've owned with a real clock on it: mandated reporting, breach notification, regulatory disclosure

  • Judgment about what's actually risky, and the willingness to say plainly when something is theater

  • Comfort reasoning from principles on questions that don't have settled regulatory answers yet

Bonus Points

  • Experience working with or inside AI labs, model providers, or platforms with similar provider relationships

  • NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, or comparable AI governance work

  • Trust and safety experience, especially mandated reporting regimes or platform integrity at consumer scale

  • Privacy engineering background

What this role is not

  • It is not a policy-writing seat. Policy is an output, not the job.

  • It is not a checkbox compliance seat. If your instinct is to close a finding by writing a
    document that says it is closed, this will not be a good fit.

  • It is not a product engineering role. If Arena builds new products in this space, they'd sit
    with their own dedicated team. This seat sets the governance and boundaries, not the roadmap.

What we offer

  • We offer competitive compensation and equity aligned to the markets where our team members are based. The base salary range will depend on the candidate’s permanent work location.

  • Comprehensive health and wellness benefits, including medical, dental, vision, and additional support programs.

  • The opportunity to work on cutting-edge AI with a small, mission-driven team

  • A culture that values transparency, trust, and community impact

Come help build the space where anyone can explore and help shape the future of AI.

Arena Intelligence provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Codes highly complex surgical, special procedures, observation records, inpatient records, medical, diagnostic, procedural, and/or recurring records within established productivity and coding accuracy guidelines. Job Summary

At Fuze Health, we put patients first and tirelessly address the most pressing needs in healthcare. We empower millions to digitally connect with care providers, essential health resources and needed treatments – and enable care providers, employers, health plans and life sciences companies to meaningfully enhance quality, outcomes and value. We are dedicated to helping our partners evolve and modernize to meet emerging patient and marketplace needs.

Fuze Health’s foundation is built upon the strategic combination of several proven, technology-powered innovators in the digital health, diagnostics, and pharmacy sectors. Our growing portfolio brings together the capabilities of industry leaders including LetsGetChecked, Truepill, and Alto Pharmacy, to create a distinctive, unified force in healthcare. Together, we have the shared vision, advanced capabilities and talented teams to deliver next-generation solutions that patients and healthcare partners need today and into the future.



Job Description

The Staff Product Manager at FuzeRx is a senior individual contributor role responsible for defining, shaping, and delivering high-impact product initiatives that advance patient care, pharmacy operations, and strategic growth. This role sits within the Product Management job family and represents the highest level of product craftsmanship and influence without direct people management.

As a Staff Product Manager, you will operate with significant autonomy, partnering closely with Engineering, Design, Clinical, Pharmacy Operations, Data, and Business leaders to solve complex problems at scale. This role is expected to set product standards, influence product strategy across domains, and mentor other Product Managers while driving measurable outcomes aligned with FuzeRx’s mission and business objectives.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own the end-to-end product lifecycle for complex, high-impact product areas, from discovery and strategy through delivery, launch, and optimization

  • Define product vision, strategy, and multi-quarter roadmaps aligned to company goals, patient outcomes, and operational efficiency

  • Partner deeply with Engineering, Design, Data, and cross-functional stakeholders to translate complex business and clinical needs into clear product requirements

  • Lead product discovery through customer research, data analysis, experimentation, and validation to ensure solutions solve real user problems

  • Drive alignment across senior stakeholders by clearly articulating tradeoffs, priorities, and outcomes using data and strong product judgment

  • Establish and monitor success metrics (KPIs/OKRs), using insights to iterate and continuously improve product performance

  • Anticipate regulatory, operational, and technical constraints in healthcare and pharmacy environments and design scalable, compliant solutions

  • Serve as a product thought leader and mentor, raising the bar for product quality, execution, and decision-making across the Product organization

Required Experience & Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, Health Informatics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in Product Management, including ownership of complex, cross-functional product initiatives

  • Experience working closely with Engineering teams in agile development environments

  • Strong analytical skills with experience defining and using product metrics to drive decision-making

  • Experience operating in regulated or highly complex domains (e.g., healthcare, pharmacy, fintech, or enterprise platforms)

  • MBA or advanced degree in Business, Healthcare Administration, Data, or a related field

  • Experience building products for pharmacy, healthcare services, life sciences, or medication management platforms

  • Experience with data-driven personalization, automation, or AI-enabled product capabilities

  • Proven track record of setting product strategy at the portfolio or platform level

  • Experience mentoring or coaching other Product Managers and contributing to product org maturity

Physical requirements for this role include the ability to work at a computer terminal with monitor, keyboard and mouse for extended periods of time, stoop, bend, and reach for equipment and supplies, make frequent repetitive motions required to operate a computer that include the wrists, hands and fingers, and lift, carry, push, pull, and move light objects up to 20 pounds. title: Broiler Serviceperson
location: Rose Hill, North Carolina, United States
description:
Service Technicians have a very important job informing contract growers and farm foremen of company policies and programs and advise them on the proper production of a healthy bird. Growers have to be informed of the company's environmental, safety, and ethical practices, and techs inspect farms for compliance with contract. Growers have to be informed of the importance of animal welfare and bio security measures. Periodically Service Techs have to help weigh birds and have to monitor the feeding of birds. Feed inventories and scheduling the feed is a job of the service Tech. A weekly account of the mortality will be reported to the accounting department. Walking through the poultry houses on a weekly basis to observe birds and to ensure all equipment is working and set properly is another duty of the tech. Birds have to be examined for evidence of disease and growth rate to determine the effectiveness of medication and feeding programs.

All service techs will attend weekly meeting and will be provided a company truck to drive on their specified routes. Communication with growers is the responsibility of the service person and will be done on a weekly basis. This is not an all-inclusive list of the duties performed by the service tech.

L3Harris is the Trusted Disruptor in defense tech. With customers’ mission-critical needs always in mind, our employees deliver end-to-end technology solutions connecting the space, air, land, sea and cyber domains in the interest of national security.

**_Job Title: Lead, Finance_** **_Job Code: 45563_** **_Job Location: Rockwall, TX, Greenville, TX, Waco, TX or Remote_** **_Job Schedule: 9/80: Employees work 9 out of every 14 days- totaling 80 hours worked- and have every other Friday off_**

**Job Description:**

The Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) Sector is seeking an experienced Finance Lead to manage the forward-pricing rates, overhead budgets and SG&A costs for the C3ISR division.

**Essential Functions:**

- Extensively analyzes Sector cost accumulation and the allocation process across divisions.
- Works under consultive direction to budget, track and report finance head count and costs in the division.
- Responsible for the Selling, General, & Administrative (SG&A) costing and roll up of costs for analysis, forecasting and reporting at the division level.
- Communicates to sector leadership for SG&A, and Budgets and Rates reporting.
- Utilize FAR and CAS standards to implement analysis and review of incurred costs through submission and audit of incurred cost proposals.
- Establish multiple department budgets for Forward Pricing Rate Proposal (FPRP) preparation, audit defense with DCMA/DCAA and cost monitoring reporting both internally and externally.
- Willingness and ability to travel up 5%.
- Ability to obtain a US Secret security clearance.

**Qualifications:**

- Bachelor’s Degree and minimum 9 years of prior relevant experience. Graduate Degree and a minimum of 7 years of prior related experience. In lieu of a degree, minimum of 13 years of prior related experience.
- Minimum 1 year experience with both the FAR and CAS to implement analysis and review of incurred costs thru submission and audit of incurred cost proposals.
- Minimum 1 year experience with indirect rate structures including multiple overhead pools, TCI G&A, Value Added G&A, abated fringe and understanding of treatment and allocation of intermediate overhead pools.
- Minimum 1 year experience with compliance understanding to review and advise on CAS410 and CAS403 disclosure statement submission, audit and defense.
- Minimum 1 year experience with SG&A costing and roll up of costs for analysis, forecasting and reporting at the division level.
- Minimum 1 year experience with establishing multiple department budgets for FPRP preparation, audit defense with DCMA/DCAA and cost monitoring reporting both internally and externally.
- Minimum 1 year experience with 3FF process for distribution of allocated costs.
- Minimum 1 year experience with SAP ERP and Hyperion systems.

**Preferred Additional Skills:**

- Compliance understanding to review and advise on CAS410 and CAS403 disclosure statement submission, audit and defense.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
- Demonstrated strong knowledge of Balance Sheet and Income Statement
- Experience in the Aerospace & Defense industry.
- Self-motivated and able to proactively solve complex problems in a timely manner.

In compliance with pay transparency requirements, the salary range for this role in California, Connecticut, Massachusetts, New Jersey, Washington, and the Greater D.C. area, Denver, or NYC areas is $105,500 - 196,500. title: Technical Lead Data Engineering
description:
About the role

We are now seekingstrategic and hands‑on data leader to guideourhigh‑performing team in delivering smarter, more efficient regulatory outcomeswhilstplayinga key role touplift processes, strengthen governance and drive reliable data solutions.

AsTechnical Lead, Data Engineeringyou willbring expertise across data architecture,datalifecycle management,AIsoftware development, information security, and agile delivery.

Key responsibilities of this role are:

  • Be accountable for the quality of data pipeline development and the flow of data on the NHVR Enterprise Data Platform. Quality is measured by data integrity, pipeline performance, uptime, efficient administration, cost, data security, data governance, and architectural integrity.
  • Own and evolve the platform architecture and technical roadmap. This includes leading the transition from notebook- and job-based pipelines toward Lakeflow declarative pipelines and other modern Databricks capabilities.
  • Own the design and continuous improvement of the metadata-driven ingestion and transformation framework. Ensure it stays scalable, maintainable, well-documented, and consistently applied.
  • Define, document, and enforce engineering standards, patterns, and practices, covering coding standards, Delta Lake and medallion design, testing, CI/CD, and observability. Ensure compliance through design reviews and code reviews.
  • Provide authoritative advice to Managers, Directors, and other senior staff across the organisation regarding architecture, augmentation, implementation, and manageability of the data on the NHVR Enterprise Data Platform.
  • Provide technical guidance, mentoring, and coaching to Data Engineers, including pairing on complex problems and building team capability in Databricks and modern engineering practice.
  • Lead technical planning within the Scrum team: break down epics, assess solution options, estimate technical effort, and identify technical risks and dependencies early.
  • Act as the technical escalation point for complex incidents, leading root cause analyses and driving lasting improvements to monitoring, alerting, and resilience.
  • Represent data engineering changes at CAB and ensure releases meet quality, security, and change management requirements.
  • Remain hands-on, delivering complex or high-risk pipeline and framework components alongside the team.

NHVR’sData Science and Analytics Unitare currently undertaking growth and considerable transformation, and this is an exciting time to join the organisation.

To learn more, the position description can be found on the NHVR Careers site - https://careers.nhvr.gov.au/jobs/search

About You

To be successful in this role you will possessa Master’s degree in information technology or computer science related or equivalent. You will have a minimum of 10 years’ experience with demonstrated skills in Databricks and Azure cloud platform (certifications in either / both would be highly regarded)

Your toolkit for success:

  • Expert Python and PySpark development skills, with advanced SQL (Spark SQL and T-SQL or similar).
  • Deep Databricks expertise, including notebooks, Jobs/Workflows, cluster configuration and policies on classic compute, and advanced Spark performance tuning.
  • Advanced Delta Lake knowledge, including MERGE and upsert patterns, schema evolution, OPTIMIZE and VACUUM, liquid clustering and partitioning strategy, and time travel.
  • Demonstrated experience designing, building, or owning metadata-driven or configuration-driven pipeline frameworks.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and implementing Unity Catalog security and governance models, including grants and ownership, row and column level security, external locations, storage credentials, and lineage.
  • Proven experience establishing approaches for identifying, classifying, and protecting sensitive and PII data.
  • Strong data architecture and modelling skills, covering relational, dimensional, and medallion architecture, normalisation, schemas, and data profiling.
  • Proven code review, software analysis, and design review skills, with a track record of defining and enforcing engineering standards.
  • Strong software engineering discipline, including modular design and design patterns, unit and data quality testing (e.g. pytest, data quality frameworks), Git-based workflows, CI/CD with Azure DevOps, and debugging.
  • Extensive experience with ELT/ETL pipelines and data integration, including REST APIs, file-based exchange (e.g. SFTP), change data capture, and streaming or event-based patterns.
  • Experience leading technical teams in Scrum and Agile methods, with the ability to mentor engineers and influence without direct authority.
  • Excellent communication skills, including explaining complex technical matters and trade-offs to senior, non-technical stakeholders

Why join us?

The National Heavy Vehicle Regulator (NHVR) commenced operations in 2013 as the national entity responsible for regulating all vehicles in Australia over 4.5 tonnes gross vehicle mass. The NHVR minimises the compliance burden on the heavy vehicle transport industry, reduces duplication and inconsistences across state and territory borders, and ultimately for the heavy vehicle business with government in Australia.

We are headquartered in Brisbane and employ more than 1000 people across the ACT, New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania and Victoria.

We offer

  • A competitive salary package of $166,662.51 per annum + Superannuation.
  • Monthly RDO and paid leave over Christmas closure.
  • Hybrid working environment – up to 2 days from home.
  • Up to15.25% superannuation through a co-contribution scheme
  • Leave loading 17.5%
  • Wellbeing programs – discounted fitness through Fitness Passport, Discount health insurance, flu vaccine, financial programs including discounted banking products, finance information sessions.
  • Salary packaging options including novated lease.
  • Discounted IT products including Microsoft and free family password security plan.
  • Ongoing training and professional development support
  • Professional membership

We are committed to being an inclusive, diverse and flexible workplace where differences are valued.We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experience and abilities.

title: Team Lead, BtoC Leasing
description:
ABOUT GREYSTAR


Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing. Headquartered in Charleston, South Carolina, Greystar manages and operates over $350 billion of real estate in more than 260 markets globally with offices throughout North America, Europe, South America, and the Asia-Pacific region. Greystar is the largest operator of apartments in the United States, managing over one million units/beds globally. Across its platforms, Greystar has nearly $79 billion of assets under management, including over $34 billion of development assets and over $36.5 billion of regulatory assets under management. Greystar was founded by Bob Faith in 1993 to become a provider of world-class service in the rental residential real estate business. To learn more, visit .

JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY

The Sales Executive is responsible for supporting marketing, leasing and occupancy/revenue objectives for Canvas by delivering activities related to leasing to new residents and renewals of existing residents. These include qualifying leads, arranging community tours and unit viewings and completing the requisite resident administration to secure the reservation.

JOB DESCRIPTION

The Opportunity

You are the engine room of the B2C leasing operation. Reporting to the Sales Manager — B2B & B2C, you are the direct manager of the centralised leasing team — up to 8 people during high season — and the person who turns strategy into daily execution. You live in the detail of the funnel: every lead, every viewing, every conversion. Your job is to keep the team productive, focused and consistently hitting target, and to make sure nothing falls through the cracks between a first enquiry and a signed lease. You lead from the floor, set the pace, and hold the standard for quality and attention to detail across every stage of the resident journey.


What You'll Drive

Lead and Manage the B2C Leasing Team

  • Act as the direct line manager for the B2C leasing team of up to 8 people during high season — owning day-to-day management, priorities, workload and scheduling.
  • Set clear daily and weekly targets for each team member and keep the team focused, motivated and accountable to them.
  • Coach and develop individuals on the floor — through call listening, viewing shadowing and real-time feedback — raising the capability and consistency of the whole team.
  • Manage shift patterns and seasonal peaks so the team is always resourced to handle demand without dropping service levels.

Drive Productivity and Maximise Results

  • Own the productivity of the B2C leasing team — monitoring output, activity levels and conversion for every individual, and stepping in quickly where performance dips.
  • Maximise conversion at every stage of the funnel, from inbound enquiry to signed lease, removing friction and chasing every opportunity to close.
  • Track individual and team KPIs daily, using the numbers to prioritise effort, reallocate resource and unlock the next incremental result.
  • Keep the team hitting occupancy and revenue targets, escalating risks and opportunities to the Sales Manager early.

Own the Detail Across the Leasing Funnel

  • Take ownership of accuracy and attention to detail across everything funnel-related — lead data, availability, pricing, tenancy documentation and CRM records.
  • Ensure every enquiry is logged, followed up and progressed on time, with no lead left unattended.
  • Maintain a clean, up-to-date pipeline and reservation record so availability and forecasting are always reliable.
  • Enforce a consistent, high-quality standard across all channels — calls, chat, email and in-person viewings — and across every piece of tenancy documentation.
  • Manage move-ins, move-outs, renewals and notices to vacate with precision, ensuring a smooth experience for every resident.

Your Profile

You are a hands-on team leader who gets results through people and detail. You are happiest close to the action — on the floor with your team, in the CRM, on top of the numbers — and you have an instinct for spotting where a lead is stalling or a process is leaking. You set a high bar, you hold it, and you bring the team with you.


Essential

  • Proven experience leading or supervising a sales, leasing or customer-service team, ideally in real estate, student housing/PBSA, hospitality or a comparable high-volume environment.
  • A track record of driving team productivity and hitting conversion, occupancy or sales targets.
  • Hands-on experience managing a leasing or sales funnel end to end, with strong attention to detail and data accuracy.
  • A natural coach who develops people through day-to-day feedback and keeps a team motivated under pressure.
  • Confident with CRM and sales tools (e.g. Yardi, Salesforce or similar) and comfortable working from KPIs and reports.
  • Highly organised, able to juggle multiple priorities and seasonal peaks without losing focus or quality.
  • Excellent communication skills and a customer-first mindset — whether the customer is a student, a parent or a colleague.
  • Fluent French and English (written and verbal); Spanish is a strong plus.

Our Values

Everything we do is guided by six core values. We don't just name them — we hire for them, live them every day, and hold each other accountable to them.

Integrity | Equality | Accountability | Professionalism | Teamwork | Service

Important Notice: Greystar will never request your banking details or other sensitive personal information during the interview process. Greystar does not conduct any interviews via text or messaging, and all communication will come from official Greystar email addresses (@greystar.com). If you receive suspicious requests, please report them immediately to AskHR@greystar.com.

title: Principal Data Engineer - Hybrid
description:
Job Description

We deliver the best GIS solutions in the world, with the brightest minds on the map.

What are the issues that matter most to you? Climate change, national security, disaster response?

At Esri Australia you'll work with people at the forefront of these issues, connect them with the best tech and solutions and get an inside look into the real-world challenges that shape our future.

We turn problems into opportunities, and that takes two things:

  • The most powerful GIS technology and solutions.
  • Driven, talented, and passionately curious people.

Here we connect them, and that’s how we achieve incredible things for communities, economies, and for your career.

About the Role

As our Principal Data Engineer, you'll play a key role in shaping the future of Esri Australia's enterprise data capability. You will provide technical leadership for our enterprise data platform while remaining hands-on in the design and delivery of modern data solutions. While this role is not customer-facing, you'll work closely with employees, business leaders and subject matter experts across the organisation to understand their needs and deliver data solutions that support better decision-making and business outcomes.

This is an opportunity to influence strategy, improve business outcomes, and build scalable, secure and reliable data services across the organisation.

Some major responsibilities:

  • Lead the evolution of Esri Australia's enterprise data architecture, platform strategy and technology roadmap.
  • Design, build and maintain scalable data platforms, pipelines, semantic models and enterprise data products.
  • Partner with business stakeholders and subject matter experts to understand priorities and co-design practical data solutions.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies, including Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake and Azure data services, to improve performance, scalability and value.
  • Drive data quality, governance, metadata, lineage and access management practices across the organisation.
  • Ensure security, privacy and compliance requirements are embedded into platform design and operations.
  • Monitor platform performance, reliability and cost efficiency while identifying opportunities for continuous improvement.
  • Collaborate with technology, cybersecurity and business teams to support integrations, releases and operational excellence.
  • Develop clear technical documentation, standards and knowledge resources that support long-term sustainability and shared ownership.
About You

You're an experienced data engineering professional who enjoys balancing strategic thinking with hands-on delivery. You can navigate complex business challenges, influence stakeholders and create practical solutions that deliver measurable value. You'll thrive in an environment where ownership, curiosity and continuous improvement are highly valued.

What we’re looking for:

  • Proven experience designing, delivering and supporting enterprise data platforms in Snowflake or similar cloud-based environments (Fabric, Databricks).
  • Strong SQL skills and experience using Python or similar scripting languages for data engineering and automation.
  • Deep understanding of enterprise data architecture, data warehousing, dimensional modelling, ETL/ELT frameworks and modern integration patterns.
  • Ability to translate business needs into well-designed, scalable and supportable data solutions.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to a range of audiences.
  • Strong knowledge of data quality, governance, observability, metadata, lineage and secure data management practices.
  • Experience working autonomously, managing competing priorities and delivering outcomes with minimal supervision.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capability with a focus on continuous improvement.
  • Relevant qualifications in Information Technology, Computer Science, Data Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent industry experience.
  • A cleared police check is required prior commencement.
  • We must hold current permanent and full-time working rights in Australia.
  • Attitude and behaviour align with Esri Australia's core values..

Discover how our values shape our impact, your journey begins with one click here: Our people.

No recruitment agencies please.

We are managing this recruitment process internally and will not accept unsolicited CVs or candidate introductions from agencies.

description:
Job Objectives

Maximizes sales and brand awareness by providing exceptional customer care to all customers in a friendly, efficient, and professional manner; gives impartial, personalized, expertise and advice regardless of brand and budget. Demonstrates a passion for beauty and wellness and provides inspirational beauty knowledge and know-how. Provides customers with solutions for their beauty and wellness needs, including mini-makeovers and skincare consultations, with an emphasis on the customers’ total look. Models and delivers a distinctive and delightful customer experience. Oversees and maintains overall beauty department standards.

Job Responsibilities/Tasks
Customer Experience
  • Engages customers by greeting them and offering assistance with products and services. Resolves customer issues and answers questions to ensure a positive customer experience.
  • Models and shares customer care best practices by proactively offering assistance, asking questions to determine customers’ needs, and informing customers of options.
  • Greets, listens, and engages customers to identify their needs, making them aware of appropriate products and services, and providing warm transfers to other areas of the store when necessary
  • Provides expertise in product demonstrations and consultations utilizing tools such as the Skin Hydrometer and tablet.
  • Leads and delivers in-store events to promote brand awareness and loyalty of Owned Brands and total Beauty, Wellness and Personal Care.
  • Builds relationships with customers; provides authentic closure of customer interaction and builds and fosters relationships.
  • Engages with omni-channel solutions to enhance customer engagement/experience.
  • Locates products in other stores or online if unavailable in the store.
Operations
  • Achieves or exceeds predetermined sales goals by assisting customers in the purchase of products and by modeling exceptional customer care.
  • Reviews beauty business on a regular basis to understand performance within store and district in partnership with store leadership.
  • Consistently focuses on link-selling and up-selling with customers by showing them sale items and complimentary offerings.
  • Uses testers and sampling to demonstrate product application and leverage items from beauty promotional programs.
  • Ensures testers are stocked and maintained in compliance with hygiene standards; maintains a clean and organized department.
  • Implements company asset protection procedures to identify and minimize profit loss.
  • Processes sales for customers and/or employee purchases on cash register.
  • Participates in meetings and conference calls concerning programs and promotions, new items, brand launches, sales goals, and modeling exceptional customer care.
  • Has working knowledge of store systems and store equipment.
  • Ensures compliance with state and local laws regarding regulated products (e.g., alcoholic beverages and tobacco products).
  • Complies with all company policies and procedures; maintains respectful relationships with coworkers.
  • Completes special assignments as assigned.
Training & Personal Development
  • Seeks self-development by monitoring own performance, setting high personal standards, maintaining awareness of beauty and wellness trends, learning from others, and improving job performance.
  • Maintains knowledge of competition, new product/brand launches, and overall industry trends
  • Attends and participates in meetings, seminars, and other knowledge and business-driving opportunities; educates store team on new beauty updates, information, and learnings from training.
  • Attends training and completes e-learning modules requested by Manager or assigned by Corporate.
  • Maintains professional appearance and image in compliance with company guidelines at all times.
  • Models and shares behavior with other Beauty and Wellness Consultants; provides training and assistance to new Beauty and Wellness Consultants.
  • Works collaboratively with Store Leadership to review goals and maintain product knowledge.

About Walgreens
Founded in 1901, Walgreens () proudly serves more than 9 million customers and patients each day across its approximately 8,000 stores throughout the U.S. and Puerto Rico. Walgreens has approximately 211,000 team members, including roughly 85,000 healthcare service providers, and is committed to being the first choice for pharmacy, retail and health services, building trusted relationships that create healthier futures for customers, patients, team members and communities.

Basic Qualifications
  • High School Diploma/GED and at least one year of experience working in a retail sales environment that required meeting a defined sales goal OR at least one year of experience proactively selling beauty or cosmetic products and providing customer care
  • Experience in developing ways to accomplish goals with little or no supervision, depending on oneself to complete objectives and determining when escalation of issues is necessary
  • Knowledge of products and brands in order to engage and meet the needs of the customer.
  • Experience building and maintaining relationships within a team.
  • Basic level PC/tablet skills.
  • Requires willingness to work flexible schedule including evenings, weekends, and holidays.
  • Must be fluent in reading, writing and speaking English. (Except in Puerto Rico)


Preferred Qualifications
  • Licensure in Cosmetology or as an Esthetician as granted by appropriate state licensing authority.
  • Experience establishing & maintaining relationships with individuals at all levels of the organization, in the business community & with vendors.
  • Experience demonstrating makeup application and providing makeovers to customers.
  • Experiencing selling Prestige brands.

  • Experience with another retailer in the form of an Externship.

### We Are Seeking

**_Team Gilbert_** has an exciting opportunity for a highly motivated professional to fill the position of **Counselor.** With every job we fill, our focus is on providing best in class service to our citizens while offering the opportunity for professional growth in a rewarding and innovative work environment.

The purpose of the Youth and Family Counselor position is to engender a higher quality of life to a diverse clientele population by providing exceptional mental and behavioral health services as a licensed clinician practicing in an outpatient counseling facility within the Gilbert Advocacy Center.  Recipients of these services include court ordered adult and juvenile offenders on diversion or probation, individuals or families experiencing a crisis or traumatic event, and victims of a crime who may be vulnerable, disenfranchised, or experiencing psycho-social stressors.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

- Provide 24/7 on-call crisis response within the community of Gilbert for a one-week shift that cycles through every 6 weeks.   On-call status requires counselors to render crisis intervention and stabilization services to victims of a traumatic event or who have lost a loved one which can include giving death notifications to next of kin.  On-call services also include triaging citizens who call or walk in the office seeking mental or behavioral health assistance.
- Perform individual therapy sessions using the Solution Focused Therapy modality.  Create treatment plans and establish goals and interventions using evidenced based practices for clients experiencing psychosocial stressors and other maladaptive thoughts and behaviors.  Ensure all clinical documentation is inputted into the electronical medical record and discharge recommendations are provided once therapy services conclude.
- Complete court ordered screenings in accordance with Arizona statute guidelines (A.A.C. Title 9, chapter 20, article 1 & 2) with adult defendants on diversion or probation who are mandated to do court ordered counseling for misdemeanor charges.  Screenings require the counselor to administer and interpret a clinical assessment tool (such as the MAST, SASSI, Mortimer Filkens, etc) to determine appropriate treatment and refer clients to approved treatment agencies to complete counseling within the categories of substance abuse, domestic violence, anger management, and mental health.
- Facilitate youth diversion programs by completing intake assessments with juvenile offenders and their parents to ascertain appropriate diversion requirements and interventions that target the incorrigible behaviors.  Run therapeutic youth groups using cognitive behavioral therapy principles to promote behavior modification and conduct follow up appointments to determine compliance satisfaction.
- [View the full job description here.](https://www.governmentjobs.com/careers/gilbert/classspecs/966985)

_Posting Closes: November 8, 2026 -_ _applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis during this period._

### About You

You are someone who effectively exceeds customer needs by building productive relationships, and taking responsibility for customer satisfaction and loyalty.  You actively participate as a member of a team to move the team toward the completion of goals and produce quality outcomes.  You are committed to our safety philosophy, and you take great pride in proactively managing time and resources to ensure that work is completed efficiently while accomplishing objectives and achieving goals beyond what is required.

At **_Team Gilbert_**, we hire innovative, forward-thinking problem-solvers who love what they do!  In addition to possessing the ability to live out our core and functional values daily, candidates must possess the following requirements

- Master's degree in social work or counseling
- 5 years of experience in conducting clinical screenings and assessments, understanding mental health disorders and providing therapy using evidence-based modalities (such as CBT, DBT, Solution Focused, etc.) and working with individuals in crisis.  Criminal justice background a plus.
- Possessing clinical knowledge and experience working with individuals with substance abuse disorders and also the dynamics of domestic violence as it relates to both the victim and offender.
- Independent LCSW or LPC license from the Arizona Board of Behavioral Health Examiners
- A valid Arizona driver's license
- Top candidates for the position will possess a positive attitude and the organizational skills needed to keep pace with a substantial work load.  They will work well in a team environment and show a lifelong commitment to continuing education.
- Must be available to work days and evenings, Monday through Thursday and be available for 24/7 On-Call shifts that generally run for a one week period every 4-6 weeks.

title: Sr Program Manager, Cybersecurity
description:
Hayward Holdings Inc. (NYSE "HAYW") is one of the leading manufacturers of residential swimming pool equipment in the world, with a significant presence in the commercial pool market that is continuously growing. Hayward designs, manufactures, and markets a full line of residential and commercial pool and spa equipment including pumps, filters, heating, cleaners, salt chlorinators, automation, lighting, safety, flow control and energy solutions at our company owned facilities. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, Hayward also has facilities in Tennessee, Arizona, and Rhode Island, Georgia, as well as Canada, Spain, France, Australia, and China.


Position Overview:

Hayward is seeking an experienced Senior Program Manager (PM) contractor to lead a strategic, multi-year cybersecurity transformation initiative. This role is responsible for overseeing complex, cross-functional programs that strengthen the organization's security posture across Enterprise IT, Operational Technology (OT), and Internet of Things (IoT) environments; manage technology risk; support regulatory and compliance requirements; and drive the remediation of security incidents, vulnerabilities, audit findings, and control deficiencies.

The Senior PM will partner closely with Cybersecurity, Infrastructure, Enterprise Applications, Legal, Internal Audit, Operations, Engineering, and other business stakeholders to develop and execute the cybersecurity transformation roadmap. This individual will establish program governance, manage executive communications, and provide regular status updates, risk assessments, and strategic recommendations to Hayward's Senior Leadership Team.

Key responsibilities include leading a comprehensive cybersecurity assessment and vendor selection process (RFP); developing and executing a multi-year cybersecurity improvement roadmap; managing cross-functional initiatives across IT, OT, and IoT environments; and coordinating incident response, risk mitigation, and remediation efforts across the enterprise. The successful candidate will possess exceptional leadership, communication, and stakeholder

management skills, along with deep experience delivering large-scale cybersecurity programs and a strong understanding of cybersecurity frameworks, governance practices, and enterprise technology environments.

Major Tasks and Responsibilities:

Cybersecurity Program Leadership:

  • Lead enterprise cybersecurity programs, initiatives, and strategic roadmaps that align with business objectives and organizational risk management priorities.
  • Establish and manage program governance, integrated plans, dependencies, decision logs, metrics, executive reporting, and escalation processes.
  • Coordinate security initiatives spanning infrastructure, cloud platforms, enterprise applications, identity and access management, data protection, vulnerability management, and third-party risk.
  • Drive the implementation and continuous improvement of security controls aligned with applicable industry standards and frameworks, such as NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 27001, CIS Controls, and SOC requirements

Incident Response and Remediation Management:

  • Provide program leadership during cybersecurity incidents by coordinating cross-functional workstreams, communications, escalations, decision-making, and recovery activities.
  • Lead post-incident remediation programs by translating findings into clearly owned corrective actions, milestones, dependencies, and measurable closure criteria.
  • Manage security findings, vulnerability remediation efforts, risk treatment plans, and audit action plans through completion and validation.
  • Facilitate post-incident reviews and lessons-learned sessions, identify root causes and control gaps, and drive sustainable process and technology improvements.
  • Prepare concise executive updates that communicate incident impact, remediation status, risks, decisions, and blockers without exposing unnecessary sensitive technical detail.

RFP, Sourcing, and Vendor Management:

  • · Lead full Cybersecurity Assessment Requests for Proposal (RFP), and vendor selection processes from requirements definition through recommendation and contracting.
  • Develop evaluation criteria, scoring models, use cases, due diligence requirements, and stakeholder review processes that support objective supplier selection.
  • Coordinate vendor demonstrations, reference checks, security assessments, commercial evaluations, and final recommendation packages.
  • Partner with Senior Leadership, IT leadership, Cybersecurity, Infrastructure, Enterprise Applications, Legal, Operations, Engineering, and other business stakeholders on contract negotiations, Statements of Work (SOWs), service-level expectations, implementation commitments, and risk provisions.
  • Manage strategic vendor relationships, performance, risks, issues, and delivery expectations throughout the program lifecycle.

Program and Portfolio Management:

  • Define program scope, objectives, success measures, deliverables, workstreams, dependencies, resources, budgets, and milestones.
  • Identify and mitigate delivery, operational, cybersecurity, compliance, third-party, and organizational change risks.
  • Provide executive-level reporting and recommendations on program health, key decisions, financial status, risks, issues, dependencies, and expected outcomes.
  • Facilitate alignment across business and technical teams and hold workstream owners accountable for commitments, decisions, and timely escalation.
  • Ensure effective change management, communications, training, operational readiness, and benefits realization are incorporated into program plans.

Audit, Compliance, and Risk Management:

  • Coordinate program activities supporting internal audits, external audits, risk assessments, penetration tests, control reviews, and compliance assessments.
  • Track remediation plans related to audit findings, security assessments, policy exceptions, control gaps, and identified risks.
  • Partner with Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, Privacy, and Cybersecurity teams to support applicable regulatory, contractual, and policy requirements.
  • Maintain clear evidence, decision records, and status documentation to support governance reviews and remediation closure.
  • Promote a culture of security awareness, accountability, and risk-based decision-making across the organization.

Requirements:

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Security, Business Administration, Project Management, or a related field.
  • 15+ years of experience managing complex technology programs, enterprise initiatives, or cybersecurity-related projects, including multiple interdependent workstreams.
  • Proven experience leading cross-functional programs involving cybersecurity, infrastructure, cloud technologies, enterprise applications, third-party vendors, OT, and IoT.
  • Demonstrated experience leading enterprise RFP processes, vendor evaluations, contract and SOW development, and strategic sourcing initiatives.
  • Experience coordinating cybersecurity incident response, crisis management, vulnerability remediation, audit remediation, or risk reduction programs.
  • Strong understanding of cybersecurity principles, technology risk management, security governance, control frameworks, and compliance practices.
  • Experience developing executive-level communications and presenting complex technical, security, and risk topics to business leaders.
  • Advanced leadership, facilitation, negotiation, conflict resolution, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent programs, ambiguity, sensitive information, and competing priorities in a global enterprise environment.
  • Working knowledge of both predictive and adaptive delivery approaches, including waterfall, agile, and hybrid program management.

Additional Preferred Qualifications:

  • Project Management Professional (PMP), Program Management Professional (PgMP), or comparable program management certification.
  • CISSP, CISM, CRISC, Security+, or another recognized cybersecurity or technology risk certification.
  • Experience with NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 27001, CIS Controls, SOC reporting, and related security or control standards.
  • Experience supporting internal and external audits, regulatory assessments, cyber insurance reviews, or customer security requirements.
  • Experience leading global programs involving multiple business units, vendors, and geographically distributed teams.

Location: Remote (needs ability to travel)

title: Technician - Ford Racing
description:
About Us

In 1901, Henry Ford designed and built the race car called “Sweepstakes.” On October 10th of that year, he drove Sweepstakes against Alexander Winton, a famous racer and builder. Against all odds Ford won. That was the beginning – “the race that changed the world” – and it continues to this day. From our victories at Le Mans in 1966 and exactly fifty years later in 2016, to multiple World Championships, the spirit of Henry Ford lives with us every day through our motorsport efforts around the world.

About the Role

The Technician plays a vital supporting role within the mechanical team, working under the direction of the No 1 Technician and Chief Mechanic to deliver high-quality preparation and maintenance of the race car. This role is hands-on, fast-paced, and critical to the success of each session, ensuring that all mechanical tasks are completed efficiently, safely, and to professional standards.

Our ideal candidate will have a proven track record of success within a top-tier motorsport team and the ability to deliver tirelessly under pressure, with professionalism and a can-do, positive attitude. This role suits an enthusiastic and capable technician who is looking to deepen their skills and contribute to a world-class racing operation.

Key Responsibilities

Car Preparation & Mechanical Support:

  • Carry out mechanical work on the assigned car, as directed by the No 1 Technician or Chief Mechanic.
  • Perform assemblies, installations, repairs, and system checks with precision and attention to detail.
  • Assist with setup changes, component replacements, and scheduled maintenance tasks.
  • Conduct basic pre- and post-session inspections and report any issues promptly.
  • Ensure accurate build spec adherence under supervision.

Workshop & Trackside Operations:

  • Support the car build, rebuild, and turnaround processes both in the workshop and at the track.
  • Assist in pit stop duties and rehearsals, performing allocated roles with accuracy and consistency.
  • Help prepare the garage, equipment, and tooling to support efficient race operations.
  • Respond quickly and professionally to instructions during high-pressure situations.

Teamwork & Communication:

  • Work closely with and take direction from the No 1 Technician, to ensure smooth workflow across the car.
  • Maintain strong communication to ensure tasks are completed correctly and on schedule.
  • Support the learning of junior team members and contribute to a positive, respectful team environment.

Continuous Improvement & Professional Conduct:

  • Participate in debriefs, reliability discussions, and learning reviews led by senior staff.
  • Maintain high professional standards for cleanliness, organisation, and conduct.
  • Continuously work on developing technical skills and motorsport knowledge.

Health, Safety & Compliance:

  • Follow all internal processes and FIA rules related to safety, working practices, and race operations.
  • Ensure tools, components, and equipment are handled safely and maintained properly.
  • Immediately highlight any safety concerns or potential risks.

Qualifications, Skills & Personal Attributes

Essential:

  • Experience as a race mechanic or technician within a professional motorsport environment.
  • Strong foundational knowledge of race car systems and mechanical principles.
  • Ability to follow instructions accurately and complete tasks to a high standard.
  • Good mechanical problem-solving skills and a proactive approach.

What You Will Do

Join the Test Solutions Engineering team within the Hardware Discipline Center at Raytheon, where we architect and build sophisticated software applications and automated test environments for mission-critical defense systems. In this role, you will develop cutting-edge software solutions that interface directly with state-of-the-art engineering hardware, supporting products across the entire lifecycle—from early lab demonstrations and design verification to high-rate production testing and long-term sustainment. Working alongside a collaborative, multi-disciplinary engineering team, you will design robust tools that ensure our nation's defense technologies perform flawlessly.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
About Silicon Labs


Silicon Labs (NASDAQ: SLAB) is the leading innovator in low-power wireless connectivity, building embedded technology that connects devices and improves lives. Merging cutting-edge technology into the world’s most highly integrated SoCs, Silicon Labs provides device makers the solutions, support, and ecosystems needed to create advanced edge connectivity applications. Headquartered in Austin, Texas, Silicon Labs has operations in over 16 countries and is the trusted partner for innovative solutions in the smart home, industrial IoT, and smart cities markets. Learn more at www.silabs.com.


Bluetooth at Silicon Labs


The Bluetooth product line represents one of the key strategic technologies and fastest growing businesses for Silicon Labs. Bluetooth is not just a standalone technology and business for Silicon Labs but it’s also a key technology part of Silicon Labs’ 802.15.4 and proprietary multi-protocol solutions. The Bluetooth team strives to be at the forefront of Bluetooth and Bluetooth mesh development and deliver first in the world, unique solutions for global tier one customers. Learn more about our Bluetooth products here: http://www.silabs.com/products/wireless/bluetooth.


Job Description


Own the technical design and delivery of complex Bluetooth stack features, from interpreting specifications and evaluating design options through implementation, validation and customer issue resolution. Make design tradeoffs across software, radio performance, power and product requirements, and guide other engineers on difficult technical decisions.


Responsibilities



  • Collaborate with the agile team and adjacent engineering teams to deliver Bluetooth low energy stack features from specification through testing and release.

  • Perform feature and feasibility analyses, designing software and APIs.

  • Implement features in embedded C using high-class design practices and coding conventions.

  • Use AI development tools where helpful for exploring solutions, writing tests, reviewing code and preparing documentation, while checking their output carefully.

  • Review designs and code, document technical decisions and help other engineers solve difficult problems.

  • Develop automated tests and measure software performance.

  • Work with build scripts, continuous integration, developer tools, technical documentation and SDK software.

  • Provide input to wireless specifications and, where relevant, participate in Bluetooth SIG working groups.

  • Debug technically demanding issues and help customers succeed with our products.

  • Provide ideas and innovations for making our products and working methods even more competitive and extraordinary.


Skills / Experience / Characteristics


Minimum 5 years of SW design and engineering experience as a SW Engineer (excluding education).



  • Experience with embedded wireless, networking software, system software, driver development or similar.

  • Additional design experience with at least some of the following: SW platforms, SW architecture, APIs, embedded systems, wireless, internet protocols, local connectivity technologies (Zigbee, Thread, Wi‑Fi), development tools, and microcontrollers (Cortex‑M, Risc‑V).

  • Positive attitude towards strong innovation, achievement, continuous technical learning, process‑orientation, and quality assurance.

  • Work experience in agile teams according to the respective methodologies is a plus.

  • Fluent written and spoken English.


Education Requirements


Preferably a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related field.


What We Offer


We offer you a key role in the IoT industry in a dynamic, fast growing and profitable company. You will also get to work with a fun and great team of top industry experts. At Silicon Labs we also care greatly about our employees and want to be a truly great place to work.

Actual base pay could vary based on factors including but not limited to experience, geographic location where work will be performed and applicant’s skill set. The base pay is just one component of the total compensation package for employees. Other rewards may include an annual cash bonus, equity package and a comprehensive benefits package.

title: ASIC Clocks Verification Engineer - New College Grad 2026
description:
NVIDIA has continuously reinvented itself over two decades. Our invention of the GPU in 1999 sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined modern computer graphics, and revolutionized parallel computing. More recently, GPU deep learning ignited modern AI — the next era of computing. NVIDIA is a “learning machine” that constantly evolves by adapting to new opportunities that are hard to solve, that only we can take on, and that matter to the world. This is our life’s work, to amplify human creativity and intelligence. Make the choice to join us today.

The GPU clocks group is looking for an exceptional ASIC Clocks Verification Engineer. The team is responsible for crafting all aspects of GPU clocking. The team collaborates with the front design team to understand the clocking requirements for the chip. The clocks team interacts with the floor-planning and back-end team to help craft the physical floorplan of the chip. The team explains the programming model to the SW team to come up with an efficient clock programming sequence. The team works with the silicon solution team to triage silicon or programming bugs in the lab.

What you'll be doing:

  • As a Clocks team member, you will be collaborating with other architects, ASIC designers and verification engineers to verify high frequency clock structures.

  • Be able to engage with multiple teams and design the GPU clock structure to satisfy all the architectural constraints.

  • Your understanding of general verification principles will be valuable to verify the clocks design.

  • Together with other team members, we deliver clock information to SOC verification team, timing and DFT teams. You will use Perl to improve the productivity of the above teams.

  • Collaborate with Software and product group to debug GPU clock silicon bugs in our new products.

  • Understand and design clocking structures to overcome sub-micron design challenges.

  • You will also identify improvements in the current design and propose and implement new ways to improve the efficiency in the GPU clocking design.

What we need to see:

  • A Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering (or equivalent experience).

  • Practical experience with SystemVerilog and Universal Verification Method (UVM).

  • Experience with Design Verification, Logic Design, and Logic Synthesis.

  • Strong coding skills in Python, Perl, or other industry-standard scripting languages.

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. Are you creative and autonomous? If so, we want to hear from you.

#LI-Hybrid

title: Quality Assurance Manager
description:
Summary

The Quality Assurance Manager leads the day-to-day quality assurance operations for the Malibu brand's manufacturing facility, managing the plant's Quality Engineers, Supplier Quality resources, Quality Supervisors, and Inspectors. This role owns in-plant quality systems, process audits, defect containment, and quality gate discipline, ensuring a proactive, prevention-focused quality organization that protects the Malibu brand and customer experience.

Key Responsibilities

Team & Operations Leadership

  • Manage and develop the plant Quality Assurance team, including Quality Engineers, Quality Supervisors, and Quality Inspectors.
  • Own staffing, training, performance management, and succession planning for the plant quality organization.

In-Plant Quality Assurance

  • Own in-plant quality systems, including process audits, layered process audits, and product inspection programs.
  • Lead nonconforming material disposition, containment, and corrective action for in-process and finished goods issues.
  • Monitor and drive plant quality KPIs (FPY, DPU, scrap, rework, warranty cost per unit).

Quality Gate & Process Discipline

  • Ensure quality checkpoints and quality gates are embedded and enforced throughout the production process.
  • Partner with Production leadership on line-side quality issues and root cause resolution.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner with the CI Site Lead, Advanced Quality Engineer, and Supplier Quality Engineer to align quality priorities and resources at the plant.
  • Represent plant quality assurance performance to brand and enterprise Quality leadership.
  • Support new product introduction and engineering change quality readiness.

Reporting & Governance

  • Ensure plant quality records, documentation, and reporting meet enterprise QMS and applicable regulatory requirements (ISO 9001, USCG/NMMA).
  • Facilitate the plant's monthly quality review with brand and enterprise leadership.

title: Principal DevOps Engineer
description:
Job Description

We're partnering with a large US financial services company to source a Principal DevOps Engineer to join them on a contract basis.

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Principal DevOps Engineer to lead the evolution of cloud, platform engineering, and operational excellence capabilities.

In this role, you will provide technical leadership in the design, implementation, and adoption of modern DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), GitOps, and AI-powered engineering practices.

You will help shape the future of software delivery by driving intelligent automation, resilience engineering, observability, and platform standardization across our engineering ecosystem.

You will partner closely with development, architecture, infrastructure, and security teams to build highly scalable, resilient, and observable platforms while improving developer productivity through self-service capabilities, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), and AI-driven operational excellence.

Reliability is engineered into everything through automation, observability, resilience testing, chaos engineering, and continuous improvement.

The Expertise You Have
  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field; master's degree preferred.
  • 9+ years of hands-on experience designing, implementing, and supporting enterprise-scale CI/CD platforms and distributed systems.
  • 3+ years of experience building and operating cloud-native solutions in AWS, including infrastructure modernization and migration initiatives.
  • 3+ years of software development experience utilizing Python, Java, or Node.js, with a strong focus on automation and software engineering best practices.
  • 2+ years of hands-on GitOps experience leveraging platforms such as Argo CD, Flux CD, or equivalent solutions.
  • Strong experience with Kubernetes and containerized application platforms.
  • Experience designing and operating highly available, distributed, service-oriented architectures.
  • Experience building and operating Internal Developer Platforms (IDPs) and enabling self-service engineering capabilities.
  • Experience utilizing AI-assisted engineering tools such as GitHub Copilot, Amazon Q, ChatGPT Enterprise, Cursor, or equivalent technologies.
  • Exposure to AIOps and Agentic AI frameworks supporting operational intelligence, automation, incident response, and workflow orchestration.
The Skills You Bring
  • Strong automation skills using Python, Shell scripting, and related technologies.
  • Deep expertise in CI/CD practices, software configuration management, automated testing, code quality analysis, and deployment automation utilizing tools such as Jenkins, Ansible, and Docker.
  • Hands-on experience with Infrastructure as Code frameworks including Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, and Ansible.
  • Strong understanding of cloud-native architectures, DevOps principles, SRE practices, and platform engineering.
  • Advanced Kubernetes administration and application delivery experience.
  • Experience with GitOps methodologies, including declarative infrastructure, automated reconciliation, progressive delivery, and version-controlled operations.
  • Hands-on experience with Argo CD, Flux CD, Argo Rollouts, or similar GitOps technologies.
  • Hands-on experience with modern observability platforms including Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana, ELK/OpenSearch, Splunk, and OpenTelemetry.
  • Strong expertise in monitoring, logging, alerting, instrumentation, and performance engineering for large-scale distributed systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to improve platform scalability, reliability, performance, and resiliency.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including incident management, root cause analysis, and troubleshooting under pressure.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to influence both technical and executive stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to collaborate effectively across diverse engineering teams and organizational boundaries.
  • Demonstrated expertise supporting mission-critical production environments with a focus on availability, reliability, and operational excellence.
  • Participation in an on-call rotation may be required.
Other preferred skills – Nice to have:
  • Experience applying AI and AIOps capabilities across software delivery, automation, monitoring, and operational workflows.
  • Familiarity with Agentic AI concepts, autonomous workflows, and AI-driven operational automation.
  • Understanding AI governance, security, compliance, and responsible AI practices.
  • Experience leveraging data analytics and visualization tools to drive operational insights.
  • Passion for continuous learning and adopting emerging technologies and best practices.
The Value You Deliver
  • Lead the adoption of GitOps and Platform Engineering practices to improve deployment reliability, scalability, governance, and developer experience.
  • Drive AI-enabled DevOps initiatives that reduce operational toil and accelerate engineering productivity through intelligent automation.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage Agentic AI capabilities for incident management, deployment validation, operational workflows, and production support within established governance frameworks.
  • Partner with engineering, architecture, infrastructure, and security teams to establish next-generation DevOps capabilities incorporating GitOps, AIOps, and AI-driven operations.
  • Accelerate software delivery while improving reliability through predictive insights, intelligent automation, and autonomous operational capabilities.
  • Support development squads with modern DevOps practices, cloud adoption, and engineering excellence initiatives.
  • Deliver high-quality, maintainable, secure, and cost-effective solutions that meet both functional and non-functional business requirements.
  • Define and execute enterprise-grade reliability and observability strategies that ensure critical systems remain highly available and performant.
  • Leverage technical, operational, and financial data to drive efficiency, reduce complexity, and eliminate manual effort.
  • Establish and promote engineering standards, platform consistency, and operational excellence across development and SRE organizations.
  • Lead troubleshooting and resolution of complex, cross-functional issues spanning applications, infrastructure, networks, and cloud platforms.
  • Mentor and coach engineers and technical leaders in reliability engineering, observability, automation, and cloud-native best practices.

title: Major Accounts Executive - West
description:
The Opportunity

Sharp Performance is hiring a Major Accounts Executive to own our largest public safety opportunities across the Western United States. These are state agencies, large county sheriff's offices, major metropolitan police and fire departments, and statewide associations. The deals are multi-stakeholder, run through formal procurement, and carry six- and seven-figure budgets.

This is a senior individual contributor role with a short list of named accounts and a high ceiling. You will run the full cycle from the first executive conversation to a signed agreement, then grow the account from there.

What You'll Own

A named territory of major public safety accounts in the West. Your job is to build executive relationships, run complex procurements, close enterprise agreements, and expand them.

How You'll Make an Impact

  • Win Enterprise Accounts: Build and close a pipeline of major agency deals. Map the buying committee, from chief and sheriff to procurement, legal, and finance, and move every stakeholder to yes.
  • Navigate Public Sector Procurement: Run RFPs, sole-source justifications, cooperative purchasing agreements, and multi-year budget cycles. You know how agency money gets approved and when.
  • Build the Business Case: Translate retention, wellness, and performance outcomes into numbers a city manager, county executive, or state budget office will sign off on.
  • Sell to the Top: Earn the trust of chiefs, sheriffs, commissioners, and association leaders. Hold the room with a full command staff.
  • Run the Deal: Keep every opportunity multi-threaded, documented, and forecast accurately in HubSpot. Your pipeline is your word.
  • Land and Expand: Lead onboarding of new enterprise customers alongside Implementations and Customer Success, then grow seats, divisions, and agencies within the account.
  • Feed the Company: Bring what large agencies need back to Product, Marketing, and leadership.

Who We're Looking For

  • Enterprise Public Safety Experience, Required: 7+ years of enterprise or major-accounts sales, including at least 3 years selling to law enforcement, fire, EMS, or other public safety agencies. You have closed six- and seven-figure agency deals and can walk us through how.
  • Procurement Fluency: Hands-on experience with government RFPs, contract vehicles, cooperative purchasing, and multi-year budgeting.
  • Executive Presence: You sell to chiefs, sheriffs, city managers, and state officials and are comfortable in the room with them.
  • Complex Deal Management: Multi-stakeholder deals with 6 to 18 month cycles, run with a proven methodology such as MEDDPICC or Challenger.
  • Track Record: Consistent quota attainment on enterprise targets. Bring the numbers.
  • Travel: Regular travel across the territory for executive meetings, site visits, and agency events.
  • Tools: HubSpot or a comparable CRM, with disciplined forecasting.

Why You'll Want to Be Here

  • Compensation: $165,000 to $185,000 base salary with on-target earnings of $355,000 to $485,000, uncapped.
  • Mission That Matters: You're not selling software to a Fortune 500. You're helping protect the mental health of cops and firefighters who need it.
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision.
  • Flexible PTO: Recharge and stay sharp, no micromanagement.
  • 401(k) with Company Match: We invest in your future.
  • Performance Coaching: Access to the same elite performance coaches we offer our clients.

title: Director, Product Management
description:
Job Summary

NetApp is seeking a Director of OEM Programs to own and expand our OEM partner ecosystem. In this role, you will work to expand Netapp’s existing partnerships, find and evaluate new ones, and design the commercial licensing models that open new routes to market. This is a high-visibility role that works with executive leadership, Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, and Sales.

Job Requirements

  • Own the strategy and P&L impact of the OEM program. Maintain and grow existing OEM partnerships through joint planning, executive engagement, and regular business reviews.
  • Work with OEM sales to Identify, evaluate, and prioritize new OEM opportunities. Build business cases covering market fit, technical integration, revenue potential, and strategic value.
  • Design and launch new commercial licensing models (for example, royalty, subscription, consumption-based, and embedded or white-label), which enable new routes to market.
  • Lead negotiation and structuring of OEM agreements, working with Legal and Finance on pricing, terms, and risk.
  • Drive partner onboarding, integration, certification, and go-to-market readiness with Engineering, Product, and Sales Operations.
  • Build and lead a team of OEM program and partner managers. Set goals, develop talent, and establish clear operating processes.
  • Define and track program KPIs, and metrics to measure the ongoing health of OEM business.
  • Serve as the escalation point for partner issues and align internal stakeholders on roadmap, support, and commercial commitments.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in OEM, channel, alliances, or strategic partnership management, including 5+ years in a leadership role.
  • Proven record of growing OEM or embedded-technology partnerships and closing complex, multi-year agreements.
  • Hands-on experience structuring licensing and pricing models and negotiating commercial terms.
  • Strong financial acumen, including revenue forecasting, deal modeling, and partner profitability.
  • Executive-level communication and relationship skills, with the ability to influence across partners and internal teams.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership across Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, and Sales.
  • Bachelor's degree required. MBA or equivalent experience preferred.

Preferred

  • Background in enterprise storage, data infrastructure, or cloud.
  • Experience with software licensing, IP, and embedded or white-label distribution.
  • Experience managing global partners across regions and time zones.
  • Success Measures
  • Growth in OEM revenue and the number of active, healthy partners.
  • New licensing models launched and adopted, opening new routes to market.
  • Partner satisfaction, renewal rates, and faster partner time to market.

Education

  • Bachelor's degree required. MBA or equivalent experience preferred.

Sales Manager
