The Member Experience Guide serves as a trusted partner to our members, owning each interaction from inquiry to resolution with empathy, clarity, and accountability. Guided by a deep sense of Member Obsession, this role puts members first in every decision, ensuring their needs are understood, prioritized, and resolved with urgency and care. Member Experience Guides embrace a Champion’s Mindset, welcoming challenges and persevering until the best possible outcome is achieved. Through courageous problem-solving and a commitment to excellence, this role reduces member effort, strengthens trust, and delivers meaningful experiences that build long-term loyalty.


You will

  • Connect with empathy and member-first focus: Build trust through active listening, acknowledging emotions, and demonstrating Member Obsession by prioritizing the member’s needs in every interaction.
  • Own the end-of-end experience: Take full accountability for resolving inquiries, requests, and concerns, navigating systems and teams with a Champion’s Mindset to achieve first-call resolution whenever possible.
  • Deliver “path to yes” solutions: Apply critical thinking and Courageous Challenge by seeking solutions beyond the obvious and addressing barriers directly to meet member needs.
  • Navigate complexity with clarity and confidence: Translate benefits, claims, and processes into simple, actionable guidance, ensuring members feel supported and informed.
  • Demonstrate tenacity and perseverance: Persist through complex or ambiguous situations, exhausting available resources before escalating and maintaining focus until resolution is achieved.
  • Provide clear next steps and follow-through: Take ownership with Resolve, set expectations and ensure closure through proactive communication and follow-up.
  • Challenge for better outcomes: Use Courageous Challenge to raise concerns, identify process gaps, and advocate for improvements that enhance the member experience.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement: Embrace Responsible Disruption by identifying opportunities to improve workflows, reduce friction, and enhance service delivery.
  • Uphold service excellence standards: Demonstrate Relentless Leadership in everyday actions by consistently delivering high-quality, empathetic, and effective service.

High School Diploma or Equivalent Experience


1+ years of customer service experience in a contact center, healthcare, hospitality, or service-oriented environment

Experience resolving customer issues, managing multiple systems, and handling high-volume interactions

Required: English (Read, Write, Spoken)

Empathy – Demonstrates the ability to recognize and validate member emotions, ensuring every interaction feels personal, respectful, and understood.

Compassion – Transforms empathy into action by proactively working to ease member concerns and improve outcomes.

Tenacity – Displays persistence and determination, embracing a Champion’s Mindset to resolve even the most complex challenges.

Resolve – Owns outcomes fully, ensuring issues are driven to closure with clear communication and follow-through.

Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, or healthcare experience

Experience in a provider office, medical group, hospital, or health plan

Hospitality or high-touch service experience

Caregiving experience demonstrating compassion and advocacy

o Spanish

title: Part-Time Office Coordinator
description:
Who We Are

Pindrop is a cybersecurity company delivering continuous identity verification across voice, video, and digital interactions. Powered by the Pindrop Intelligence Network, our unified trust platform helps enterprises answer three critical questions:

Is this identity synthetic? Detect AI-generated and manipulated voice and video.
Is this identity risky? Identify fraud, suspicious behavior, and other risk signals.
Is this identity known? Authenticate identities using voice, device, behavioral, and other signals.

Pindrop brings this intelligence together across purpose-built trust engines to help organizations make informed decisions in real time — protecting customers, workforce interactions, and emerging AI-driven interactions.

Pindrop protects billions of high-risk interactions for enterprises, including leading financial institutions, insurers, and healthcare organizations. Its technology is informed by more than 8 billion real-world interactions annually and protected by 300+ patents.

Recognized by TIME as one of the 10 Most Influential Software Companies of 2026 and by Inc. for Best in Business for Innovation, Pindrop is backed by leading investors including Andreessen Horowitz, IVP, and CapitalG.

Part-Time Office Coordinator

ATLANTA, GA | PINDROP HEADQUARTERS | ON-SITE

Looking for a flexible, part-time role where you can make a real impact and get a front-row seat to life inside a growing AI company? Ever seen The Intern? Think that… but at an AI company.

This might be the perfect role for you!

At Pindrop, we’re looking for someone to help keep our Atlanta headquarters running smoothly and make the office a place people genuinely enjoy coming to.

You’ll meet some pretty incredible people and experience all the joys of office life. Yes, that includes meetings, calendars, conference rooms, and the occasional mystery package.

But note: we’re looking for someone who takes the little things seriously.

Someone who is exceptionally responsible, ridiculously detail-oriented, and has a genuine service mindset. The kind of person who notices the coffee is running low before it’s gone, remembers that someone has a dietary restriction, and takes pride in making everyone else’s day a little easier.

Corporate experience isn’t required. You do need great judgment, a positive attitude, and the ability to own your responsibilities without someone constantly reminding you.

What You’ll Be Doing

Be the person who keeps everything running.

  • Manage incoming and outgoing mail, packages, and deliveries.
  • Keep our office stocked with snacks, drinks, coffee, and supplies. (Yes, people take their snacks seriously.)
  • Track inventory, manage orders, and stay within budget.
  • Keep our meeting rooms organized, stocked, and ready for action.

Own Wednesday Lunch.

Wednesday is our main in-office day, and we provide lunch for the team. You’ll be the mastermind behind making it happen.

  • Coordinate weekly lunch orders, vendors, headcounts, and dietary needs.
  • Make sure food arrives on time and everything is set up beautifully.
  • Handle cleanup and all the little details that make the experience great.
  • Occasionally become everyone’s favorite person in the office.

Help us create a great office experience.

  • Coordinate with building management, cleaning services, and other vendors.
  • Help organize catering and logistics for meetings and special events.
  • Manage parking access for employees and visitors.
  • Keep our shared spaces welcoming, organized, and functioning.
  • Spot things that need attention and take initiative to get them resolved.

Who We’re Looking For

Let’s talk about what really matters to us.

  • You’re exceptionally dependable. If you say you’re going to do something, it gets done. No chasing, no reminding, no wondering.
  • Details are your thing. You notice what others miss, and you genuinely enjoy making sure everything is just right.
  • You have a service heart. You like helping people. Not because it’s in your job description, but because making someone’s day better makes yours better too.
  • You’re proactive. You don’t wait to be told the coffee is empty, the conference room is messy, or the lunch order needs to be placed.
  • You’re organized and resourceful. You can juggle multiple responsibilities, manage a budget, solve small problems independently, and know when to ask for help.
  • You bring a positive attitude. You’re friendly, approachable, professional, and comfortable interacting with everyone from new employees to senior executives.

Prior experience in hospitality, customer service, administration, or office coordination is a plus, but attitude, accountability, and attention to detail matter more to us than your résumé.

The Details

  • Location: Pindrop Headquarters, Atlanta, GA
  • Schedule: Part-time, approximately 12+ hours per week
  • Wednesdays are required: This is our primary in-office day, and we need you there to make the magic happen.
  • Flexibility: Other scheduled days may vary based on office needs.
  • On-site: This is a hands-on, in-person role.
  • Essential functions: Moving around the office, standing for portions of the day, and lifting and carrying packages up to 25 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Why This Could Be a Great Opportunity

Whether you’re exploring a new field, returning to the workforce, supplementing other work, or simply want a flexible role, you’ll get exposure to how a growing AI company operates, build relationships across the organization, and develop skills that travel with you wherever your career takes you.

One Last Thing…

We’re a technology company, but this is very much a people role.

We’re looking for someone who understands that great employee experiences are often built on the smallest details.

If you’re the person who naturally takes charge of organizing the group dinner, notices when something is out of place, follows through on every commitment, and genuinely enjoys taking care of others…

We’d love to meet you.

Come see what it’s like to be part of a growing AI company. We promise it’s not all spreadsheets and meetings. 😉

Pindrop is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all ages, backgrounds, and experience levels.

Please note that the base pay range is a general guideline only. Pindrop considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, a candidate's work experience, education/training, and key skills, as well as market and business considerations, when extending an offer.

US Base Pay Range
$30—$30 USD

Not sure if this is you?

We want a diverse, global team, with a broad range of experience and perspectives. If this job sounds great, but you’re not sure if you qualify, apply anyway! We carefully consider every application and will either move forward with you, find another team that might be a better fit, keep in touch for future opportunities, or thank you for your time.

AI - A Transformative Force

At Pindrop, we view artificial intelligence as a transformative force that, when harnessed responsibly, can unlock unprecedented value for our customers, partners and society and enable and empower us to continue to deliver cutting-edge technology to combat fraud and unblur the lines between what it means to be human versus machine.

Applications with the strongest match to job requirements are prioritized for human review; not all applications may be individually reviewed.

Pindrop is an Equal Opportunity Employer

Here at Pindrop, it is our mission to create and maintain a diverse and inclusive work environment. title: Grocery Floor Clerk
description:
About Us

Join us at WinCo Foods, where we're more than just a grocery retailer - we're a growing family of over 140 supermarkets in 10 states with over 22,000 employee owners. Our purpose is to make the lives of our customers and employee owners better by offering the lowest possible prices to feed their families. Currently, WinCo is the second largest Employee-Owned company in the United States. With more than 500 millionaire employee-owners in our Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP). Our benefits, including top-tier medical plans and tuition support set us apart. In your role, you'll be instrumental in making a real impact in the communities we serve, embodying our purpose every day.

Overview

Job Summary

Provide customer service by processing customer orders in an efficient, accurate, safe and courteous manner. Consistently provides friendly, courteous customer service to internal and external customers. Performs other related work. Generally works 6-8 hour shifts between 4:00 am and 1:00 am.

Typical Duties and Responsibilities

  • Seeks opportunities to welcome, engage, serve and thank customers. Maintains an atmosphere of friendly, enthusiastic customer service with an emphasis of taking care of the customer.
  • Maintains an atmosphere of enthusiastic customer awareness with an emphasis on fast, friendly customer service.
  • Operates check stand equipment such as a cash register, scanner and scale to process customer orders using two aisles to check customers.
  • Engages in suggestive selling and other sales techniques.
  • Processes monetary transactions (i.e., giving and receiving change, etc.) including cash, checks, gift certificates, travelers checks, food stamps, processing coupons, and refunds.
  • Maintains knowledge of current product location, monitors UPC codes and ensures proper pricing.
  • Maintains clean, neat and properly stocked check stand and ensures safe and secure work area.
  • Stocks, prices and rotates merchandise.
  • Performs other duties as assigned or needed.

Requirements

Ability to:

  • Work varied shifts in a 24/7 operation; including night, weekends and holidays.
  • Perform friendly, courteous, tactful relations with customers and co-workers with composure.
  • Communicate (hearing and speech) to perform customer relation skills.
  • Complete written forms.
  • Conduct visual inspection, read information on merchandise, etc.
  • Lift and maneuver objects of varying dimensions and weights up to 20 lbs. frequently and perform repetitious work accurately.
  • Lift up to 50 lbs. occasionally.
  • Operate check stand equipment such as cash registers, scanners, and scales.
  • Stand for long periods of time, walk rapidly, bend, stoop, twist, and turn frequently for long periods of time.
  • Manual dexterity and good hand/eye coordination.
  • Learn and memorize a considerable amount of information including PLU codes, location of products, check stand and keyboard procedures and company policies.
  • Ensure accuracy in recording sales and handling monetary transactions with mental alertness and basic math skills (add, subtract, multiply and divide).
  • Climb and balance on ladders when stocking shelves.
  • Use blades for box cutting.
  • Work in a cooler and freezer.
  • Use household cleaners to maintain work area (i.e., waxes, glass cleaner, etc.).
  • Work in varying weather conditions for performance of outdoor duties.
  • Must be 16 years of age or older.
  • Perform primary duties efficiently and accurately.

Additional Requirements:

  • Food Handlers Certification (Per State Laws)

Machines and Equipment Operated:

  • Fork lift, electric and manual pallet jacks, hand truck, garbage and card board compactor.
  • Box knife

For minors hired, hours may differ as well as machines and equipment operated.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature of work performed by the employees assigned to this job. All employees must comply with Company policies and applicable laws. The responsibilities, duties and qualifications required of personnel may vary.

EEO/Inclusivity

As the WinCo Foods community continues to grow, our variety of perspectives and wide range of experiences are essential to our strategy and success. We are committed cultivating and celebrating an inclusive environment in which all employees are valued and respected.

**Job Title: Government Compliance Senior Specialist**

**Job Code: 45052**

**Job Location: Remote**

**Job Schedule: 9/80 (Every other Friday off)**

**Job Description:**

This role requires strong knowledge of Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), Cost Accounting Standards (CAS), and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS). The Senior Specialist is responsible for preparing and submitting annual Incurred Cost Proposals (ICP) and supporting the development of Forward Pricing Rate Proposals (FPRP), ensuring accuracy and timeliness in accordance with regulatory requirements. The position supports all phases of DCAA audits — including incurred cost, forward pricing, CAS, and business systems audits — from readiness through resolution while maintaining productive working relationships with government auditors and implementing sustainable corrective actions. The Senior Specialist owns the CAS Disclosure Statement, including preparing revisions, identifying cost accounting practice changes, and developing cost impact analyses. Additionally, this role advises internal stakeholders on FAR Part 31 Cost Principles, collaborating closely with various functions, including Finance, Accounting, and Estimating teams, to ensure all costs charged to government contracts are allowable, allocable, and reasonable. The position also plays a key educational role within the organization, conducting compliance training for employees on topics such as labor charging, DFARS business systems, and government audit processes.

**Essential Functions:**

• Prepare annual Incurred Cost Proposals (ICP) and ensures timely submittal

• Support the preparation and submittal of Forward Pricing Rate Proposals (FPRP)

• Support all phases of DCAA audits (ICP, FPRP, CAS, business systems, etc.) from readiness activities to resolutions

• Provide guidance on FAR/DFARS requirements, cost accounting standards, and other government accounting and compliance topics to supported organizations

• Responsible for the CAS Disclosure Statement, including preparing and submitting revisions, identifying cost accounting practice changes, and preparing cost impact analyses

• Ensure consistency between disclosed and actual practices

• Manage government auditor relationships, negotiates audit findings, and implements sustainable corrective actions

• Advise on FAR Part 31 Cost Principles and collaborates closely with Finance, Accounting, and Estimating teams to ensure all direct and indirect cost charges to government contracts are allowable, allocable, and reasonable

• Conduct training sessions for employees on compliance subjects such as labor charging, DFARS business systems, and government audits

• Lead/support ad hoc requests and special projects regarding compliance matters

• Interface with DCMA (DACOs/ACOs), DCAA auditors, and customers as required

**Qualifications:**

• Bachelor’s Degree and a minimum of 6 years of prior relevant experience; Or, Graduate Degree and a minimum of 4 years of prior related experience; Or, in lieu of a degree, a minimum of 10 years of prior related experience

• Demonstrated knowledge of reconciliation of financial statements, schedule organization and indirect rate pools, and support documentation requirements

• Strong understanding of projected indirect rates and base and pool development

• Strong government accounting knowledge and experience at a defense contractor or government agency, including experience with FAR (Federal Acquisition Regulations) and working with DCMA (Defense Contract Management Agency) and DCAA (Defense Contract Audit Agency)

description:

Job Description:

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

Electrification + Energy Solutions (E+ES):

Caterpillar’s Electrification + Energy Solutions (E+ES) Division focuses on delivering advanced electrified power train, zero-emissions products/technologies, and the solutions and services associated with these technologies. Focus areas include batteries, fuel cells, motors, inverters, micro grid controllers, charging, energy storage systems, lifecycle solutions/services and integration of components for ePowertrain solutions across industries.

We are looking for top talent to build and scale the next generation of technologies, products and services to help our customers build a better—more sustainable—world. We need self-motivated, intelligent and team-oriented individuals to make our plans a reality. Individuals with high emotional intelligence, humility and openness to discovery will thrive in the teams we are building.

What You Will Do (including but not limited to):

  • Sets up, operates, and adjusts machines to perform a variety of functions to manufacture, assemble, and test stators and propulsion modules for electric drives.

  • Locate, identify and use proper fixtures and tooling to set-up and operate automatic MIG and Plasma weld machines. Repair non-standard weld flaws, conduct pre and post inspection on all welds.

  • Use blueprints, gages, torque measuring devices and/or other equipment to ensure conformance to quality specifications.

Including the operation of process chambers with hydraulically operated door and locking ring Monitor electric curing ovens, vacuum, pumping systems, chiller/circulation pump systems and low speed agitators.

title: Vice President of Administration
description:
Vice President of Administration

Reports to: President and CEO

Supervises: Director of Administration; Administration Coordinator (upon hire); Manager of Office Services

Status: Full-time, Exempt

Leadership body: Leadership Team

Classification: Band 7

Revised date: September 2026

Position Summary

The Vice President of Administration is a member of the Leadership Team responsible for the systems, infrastructure, and people-and-culture practices that let Alaska Community Foundation run smoothly, efficiently, and sustainably. The role combines operational stewardship with human-resources leadership, and holds executive accountability for ACF's key operating vendor relationships.

The VP of Administration oversees the Director of Administration, whose branch manages day-to-day facilities operations, including the BP Energy Center; the Manager of Office Services (Michele Murphy), who owns general office administration, front-desk operations, staffing and resource logistics, and supply and equipment management, distinct from facilities work; and, once the position is filled, the Administration Coordinator, who provides cross-functional coordination and execution support.

Key Responsibilities

Operations, Compliance, and Vendor Management

  • Lead and continuously improve administrative systems and operations, including HR, IT, office management, and facilities.
  • Serve as executive liaison to ACF's key operating vendor relationships, including the external human resources partner and Resource Data (IT vendor), holding those partnerships accountable for service and value at the contract level; day-to-day IT support sits with the Director of Administration.
  • Oversee vendor relationships, insurance, and contracts, and ensure compliance with employment law and other operational regulations.
  • Develop and manage departmental budgets and operational policies.

Office Services

  • Hold executive accountability for staff, equipment, supplies, and other administrative resources being managed and allocated effectively across the organization; day-to-day office administration and logistics sit with the Manager of Office Services.
  • Set priorities and direction for the Office Services function, distinct from facilities management.

Facilities and BP Energy Center Oversight

  • Hold executive accountability for the BP Energy Center, the Foundation's community event facility, ensuring it remains welcoming, well-maintained, and mission-aligned; day-to-day management sits with the Director of Administration.
  • Set the direction for equitable rental and usage policy for nonprofits and community partners.
  • Ensure the facility supports local collaboration, learning, and community visibility.

People and Culture

  • Direct HR strategy and practice (hiring, onboarding, performance management, and compliance) in partnership with ACF's external HR consultant.
  • Build and sustain a positive, inclusive organizational culture grounded in the Foundation's values.
  • Partner with Leadership Team peers on staff learning and professional development.
  • Ensure HR practices stay current, equitable, and compliant with applicable law and standard.

Team and Operational Leadership

  • Lead and develop the Director of Administration, the Manager of Office Services, and, once seated, the Administration Coordinator.
  • Develop and manage departmental budgets, work plans, and performance metrics.
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, learning, and continuous improvement across the function.
  • Ensure operational systems and tools effectively support the work of every department.

Leadership Team Participation

  • Serve as an active member of the Leadership Team, contributing to organization-wide strategy, planning, and decision-making.
  • Partner with fellow Leadership Team members on cross-functional collaboration and alignment.
  • Advise the CEO and Board on internal operations, organizational infrastructure, and people-and-culture matters.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in business, public administration, or a related field preferred.
  • 7+ years of progressively responsible leadership experience in operations, administration, or organizational management.
  • Demonstrated experience in HR management, facilities oversight, and organizational systems.
  • Working knowledge of employment law and HR compliance, insurance, and contract administration, with experience managing vendor relationships.
  • Excellent interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to maintain strict confidentiality and exercise sound judgment.
  • Knowledge of and commitment to Alaska, its communities, and the mission of ACF.

Core Competencies

  • Operational systems leadership and infrastructure management.
  • Human resources and people-and-culture stewardship.
  • Vendor portfolio management and executive-level accountability.
  • Facility oversight through a direct report.
  • Executive leadership and organizational contribution.
  • Team development and organizational effectiveness.
  • Cross-functional collaboration and commitment to a mission-aligned workplace.

Work Environment and Accessibility

We are committed to creating an inclusive and accessible workplace. The physical, sensory, and environmental requirements described here represent the general nature of the role and are not intended to exclude individuals who can perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

This role is primarily desk-based work in a professional office environment. The position requires the ability to effectively engage in communication, operate standard office technology or job-related equipment, and perform the core responsibilities of the role.

Reasonable accommodations will be provided in accordance with applicable laws to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

title: Senior Avionics Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
TYTAN Technologies

At TYTAN, we aim to set a global standard in autonomous air defense with AI-driven, cost-efficient systems that counter unmanned aerial threats at scale. We protect people. We protect critical infrastructure. We protect European sovereignty.

We are looking for a Senior Avionics Engineer to define, implement, and validate the avionics architecture of advanced UAV platforms. You will be responsible for integrating autonomy, GNC, and command & control (C2) into a coherent, reliable onboard system across fixed-wing, VTOL and transitioning aircrafts.

This role is hands-on, system-level, and deployment-focused. You will work at the intersection of hardware and software, ensuring that all onboard systems communicate reliably and perform in real operational environments. You will act as a technical sparring partner across avionics and system integration, contributing experience, pragmatism, and strong engineering judgment.

Your roadmap to make an impact

  • Define and own the end-to-end avionics architecture for UAV platforms, from concept to operational deployment

  • Define and implement system-level integration of flight control (GNC), autonomy stacks, and C2 links

  • Design and manage onboard communication architectures (e.g., MAVLink, DDS, Ethernet, CAN, serial protocols)

  • Integrate and validate flight controllers, companion computers, sensors, radios, and payload systems

  • Ensure robust data flow, synchronization, and fault-tolerant behavior across all subsystems

  • Take avionics systems from lab setup to real aircraft, ensuring reliable sim-to-real and bench-to-flight transition

  • Lead and support hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and system-level testing, including debugging complex integration issues

  • Work closely with GNC, autonomy, C2, and EWIS/electrical teams to ensure tight system coupling and clean interfaces

  • Support flight testing, including system bring-up, monitoring, logging, and post-flight analysis

  • Define and implement system monitoring, health checks, and fail-safe strategies

  • Document system architectures, interfaces, and integration workflows in a clear and maintainable way

  • Support integration into customer and operational environments, including Bundeswehr (Bw) requirements


  • 5+ of hands-on experience in avionics, robotics, or UAV system integration

  • Strong experience working with real UAV systems, ideally across fixed-wing and/or VTOL platforms

  • Proven track record of integrating complex systems (flight controllers, companion computers, sensors, radios) into a working aircraft

  • Strong understanding of system architecture, interfaces, and real-time data flow

  • Experience with autopilot systems (e.g., PX4) and UAV software stacks

  • Proficiency in C++ and Python, with practical experience in ROS2 or similar middleware

  • Hands-on experience with communication protocols (e.g., MAVLink, CAN, UART, Ethernet, DDS)

  • Comfortable debugging hardware-software integration issues in real systems

  • Experience with Linux-based systems, embedded computing, and system bring-up

  • Strong systems-thinking mindset: understanding of how everything connects and fails together

Nice to have

  • Experience with C2 systems and radio link integration, including bandwidth and latency considerations

  • Experience with HIL/SIL testing setups and simulation integration

  • Experience supporting flight testing and field deployments

  • Background in defense or safety-critical systems

Why TYTAN?

  • Build technology with real operational impact: Develop autonomous defence systems designed to protect lives and strengthen Europe’s security

  • Shape scalable defence capabilities: Work on solutions built for mass deployment, cost efficiency, resilience, and reliable production at scale

  • Contribute to networked air defence: Help integrate our systems into multi-layered defence architectures alongside sensors, command systems, and effectors

  • Develop for real-world operations: Build capabilities together with end users and improve them continuously based on direct operational feedback

  • Move fast and take ownership: Work in a focused, high-performance team where decisions are made quickly and individual contributions have immediate impact

  • Define a new generation of defence technology: Join early and help shape the products, engineering standards, culture, and direction of a fast-growing deep-tech company

  • Work with an international mission-driven team: Collaborate with experienced specialists united by the goal of creating sovereign and effective security capabilities for Europe

Our Benefits

  • Virtual stock options: Participate in our success through Virtual stock options (VSOPs) at the company's current valuation

  • Monthly allowances: €106/month in flexible benefits including lunch discounts and EGYM Wellpass or shopping credit

  • Regular health care events: Health check-ups, skin screenings, mental health workshops, and an annual vitamin infusion on us

  • Referral bonus: Earn a reward when someone you refer joins the team

  • Regular team events: On- and off-site activities to connect and celebrate together

  • Corporate discounts: Exclusive employee discounts across a wide range of partner brands

  • Flexibility: Flexible working hours and hybrid work model, plus a modern Munich office built for focus and collaboration

  • Dynamic and fast-paced team: Be among the first to shape a deep-tech defence company redefining the future of security with an international team where your impact is immediate

About us

At TYTAN, it is more than just a job; it is about embracing autonomy, personal growth, and purpose. Make a lasting impact in the new era of defense! Join us to create a safer world for all.

WE are an equal-opportunity employer committed to fairness and inclusivity. We do not prioritize any specific religion, gender, nationality, or background. Due to security clearance requirements, affiliations with countries listed under § 13 para. 1 no. 17 SÜG may affect the application process.

Please note that we currently do not offer visa sponsorship, so we’re only able to consider candidates who already have a valid work permit. All qualified applicants are hereby encouraged to apply.

description:
Hakuaika päättyy 19.10.2026

HELSINKI

Etsimme AI & Analytics -yksikköömme kokenutta ja ihmisläheistä Head of Data Engineeringia johtamaan data engineering -organisaatiotamme sekä kehittämään data-alueen osaamista, toimintamalleja ja tulevaisuuden kyvykkyyksiä. Työskentelypaikkanasi on Helsingin toimistomme Vallilassa, jossa kohtaamme kollegoidemme kanssa useamman kerran viikossa. Työtehtävien salliessa voit myös joustavasti työskennellä etänä osan viikosta.

Millaisesta tehtävästä on kyse?

AI & Analytics -yksikkömme vastaa S-ryhmän tekoäly-, analytiikka- ja datakyvykkyyksien kehittämisestä. Head of Data Engineeringina johdat data-aluetta kompetenssiorganisaatiossa ja varmistat, että liiketoiminnoillamme on käytössään oikea osaaminen, resurssit ja teknologiat liiketoiminnan tavoitteiden saavuttamiseksi. Roolissa toimit oman noin 10 henkilön tiimisi esihenkilönä sekä kolmen data-alueen esihenkilön esihenkilönä.

Tehtävässä vastaat erityisesti osaajien saatavuudesta, henkilöstöjohtamisesta sekä data-alueen pitkäjänteisestä kehittämisestä. Data-alueeseen kuuluu data engineering työn lisäksi data- ja ML-alustat, joita käytetään läpi kaikkien liiketoimintayksiköiden.

Tehtävän tavoitteena on keskittää data-alueen henkilöstö- ja hallinnollisia vastuita tähän rooliin, jotta muut esihenkilöt voivat keskittyä entistä vahvemmin kompetenssien, teknologioiden ja toimintatapojen kehittämiseen. Pääset ratkomaan muun muassa seuraavia kysymyksiä:

  • Miten rakennamme data-aluetta vastaamaan liiketoimintojen tulevia tarpeita?
  • Miten varmistamme oikean tasapainon sisäisen osaamisen ja ulkoisten kumppanien välillä?
  • Miten vahvistamme data-alueen osaamista, kulttuuria ja toimintamalleja pitkäjänteisesti?
  • Miten hyödynnämme uusia teknologioita tehokkaasti, turvallisesti ja kustannustehokkaasti?

Keskeisiä sidosryhmiäsi ovat liiketoimintojen toiminnallisten tiimien vetäjät ja tuoteomistajat, kehitysjohtajat, muut AI & Analytics -yksikön tiimien vetäjät, teknologiayksikön johtajatsekä HR. Vastuullasi ovat muun muassa rekrytoinnit, resursoinnin suunnittelu, urapolkujen kehittäminen, palkitsemisen linjakkuuden varmistaminen yhdessä team leadien kanssa sekä esihenkilöiden tukeminen henkilöstöasioissa. Lisäksi osallistut data-alueen vision, strategisen suunnan ja yhteisten toimintatapojen kehittämiseen.

Minkälaista osaajaa etsimme?

Toivomme sinulta vahvaa kokemusta esihenkilötyöstä sekä näyttöjä laajojen asiantuntijaorganisaatioiden johtamisesta. Sinulla on kokemusta modernista tuoteorganisaatiosta, kompetenssikeskusmallista sekä ketteristä toimintatavoista. Olet onnistuneesti kehittänyt uusia toimintamalleja ja vienyt muutoksia käytäntöön yhdessä eri sidosryhmien kanssa.

Lisäksi odotamme sinulta vahvaa teknistä data engineering -taustaa sekä käytännön kokemusta moderneista datateknologioista, kuten AWS, Snowflake, data laket, dbt, datakatalogit ja -sopimukset, Python ja Terraform, vaikka hands-on työ olisikin viime aikoina ollut vähäistä. Ohjelmistokehitystausta katsotaan eduksi.

Etsimällämme henkilöllä on erityisesti seuraavia vahvuuksia:

  • Ihmisten ja osaamisen johtaminen: Osaat johtaa kokeneita asiantuntijoita ja esihenkilöitä, kehittää osaamista pitkäjänteisesti sekä luoda edellytyksiä onnistumiselle koko organisaatiossa.
  • Strateginen ajattelu ja visionäärisyys: Kykenet muodostamaan näkemyksen data-alueen tulevaisuudesta ja rakentamaan suunnan, joka tukee liiketoiminnan muuttuvia tarpeita.
  • Liiketoimintalähtöisyys: Ymmärrät, miten data engineering mahdollistaa liiketoimintahyötyjä, ja osaat käydä vaikuttavaa vuoropuhelua myös ei-teknisten sidosryhmien kanssa.
  • Muutosjohtaminen ja jatkuva parantaminen: Innostut uusista toimintatavoista, johdat muutoksia määrätietoisesti ja autat organisaatiota kehittymään jatkuvasti.
  • Vuorovaikutus- ja yhteistyötaidot: Rakennat luottamusta eri sidosryhmien välillä, ennaltaehkäiset konflikteja ja viet asioita eteenpäin yhteistyössä muiden kanssa.

Miksi valita meidät?

Tässä roolissa pääset vaikuttamaan koko S-ryhmän data engineering -kyvykkyyksien kehittämiseen sekä rakentamaan organisaatiota, jonka työ näkyy laajasti liiketoiminnoissamme. Saat mahdollisuuden johtaa kokeneita asiantuntijoita ja esihenkilöitä sekä olla keskeisessä roolissa määrittämässä data-alueen tulevaisuuden suuntaa. Lisäksi:

  • Hyvästä ja tuloksellisesta tekemisestä palkitaan, ja meillä jokainen työntekijä on tulospalkkauksen piirissä.
  • Saat käyttöösi Suomen laajimmat henkilöedut, mikä tarkoittaa alennuksia ruoasta, ravintoloista, hotelleista, elektroniikasta, meikeistä, kurahousuista, kodinkoneista tai vaikkapa autopesusta. Meillä työskennellessä elämä työn ulkopuolella on vähän helpompaa ja paljon hauskempaa. Eduistamme voit lukea lisää TÄÄLTÄ.
  • S-ryhmä on Suomen suurin yksityinen työnantaja, joten täältä eivät mahdollisuudet lopu. Meillä urapolut ovat usein pitkiä, toisinaan mutkittelevia, mutta aina mahdollisuuksia täynnä.

Me S-ryhmässä olemme sitoutuneet työskentelemään monimuotoisen ja syrjimättömän työympäristön puolesta, jossa kunnioitetaan ja arvostetaan kaikkien työntekijöidemme ainutlaatuisia taustoja, taitoja ja näkemyksiä.

title: Senior Data & AI Engineer
description:
CareDx is a leading precision medicine diagnostics company advancing care in transplant, specialty oncology, and cell therapy. Through our innovative portfolio of molecular diagnostics, digital health solutions, AI-powered data and analytics, and patient support services, we partner with healthcare providers, patients, and biopharma organizations to help inform clinical decision-making and improve patient outcomes.

At CareDx, every employee has the opportunity to contribute to innovations that help transform patient care and improve lives.

The Senior Data and AI Engineer will serve as a senior hands-on technical owner for solutions that transform structured and unstructured data from real-world electronic medical records (EMRs) into reliable, standardized clinical data. The role will design and deliver data engineering and clinical natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to integrate, identify, and normalize diseases, diagnoses, laboratory tests and results, demographics, signs and symptoms, medications, procedures, and other information supporting clinical, scientific, and business operations.

This role combines data engineering, clinical NLP, medical terminology and ontology expertise, applied AI, OMOP data modeling, and production software engineering. The engineer will harmonize structured EMR data, interpret clinical narratives, and integrate these sources into a transplant-focused OMOP Common Data Model (CDM). Success requires sound technical judgment, strong clinical domain knowledge, close collaboration with clinicians, and ownership from data integration and validation through deployment and ongoing production support.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the design, implementation, testing, deployment, and maintenance of pipelines that integrate structured EMR data and process unstructured clinical narratives.
  • Develop entity and relationship extraction workflows for diagnoses, symptoms, laboratory results, demographics, medications, allergies, and procedures, linking findings to relevant values, units, doses, routes, frequencies, anatomical sites, and dates.
  • Normalize structured source codes and extracted clinical concepts using ICD, SNOMED CT, RxNorm, LOINC, and other appropriate terminologies; manage local codes, synonyms, abbreviations, ambiguous mappings, terminology versions, and hospital-specific language.
  • Implement clinical context interpretation, including negation, uncertainty, temporality, experiencer, and treatment status. Distinguish current conditions from historical, family, hypothetical, and ruled-out findings.
  • Handle clinical note structure, copied-forward content, conflicting statements, and information spanning sentences or encounters. Reconcile extracted findings with structured EMR records using defined source and time precedence rules while retaining discrepancies, source evidence, and clinical timelines.
  • Build and evaluate hybrid approaches using rules, dictionaries, statistical or deep learning models, and LLMs; apply structured output validation and terminology checks to prevent unsupported facts and invalid codes.
  • Partner with clinicians to define clinical data schemas, source mappings, annotation guidelines, reference datasets, and acceptance criteria; resolve annotation disagreements and translate clinical requirements into engineering specifications.
  • Measure entity, relationship, assertion, and normalization performance; conduct clinical error analysis and validate generalization across hospitals, specialties, and note types using patient-level data separation and checks for data leakage.
  • Preserve source text, note and encounter identifiers, extraction provenance, model and terminology versions, and review status. Establish confidence thresholds and human review workflows for ambiguous or high-impact outputs.
  • Build ETL workflows, APIs, and validation controls to harmonize structured EMR fields and NLP outputs, including patient and encounter linkage, units, timestamps, and duplicate records; monitor data quality, throughput, reliability, and model performance, and resolve production issues.
  • Document architecture and operational procedures, lead code and design reviews, mentor engineers, and communicate technical tradeoffs to clinical, scientific, product, and engineering stakeholders.
  • Follow security, privacy, and compliance requirements for sensitive healthcare data, including HIPAA-aligned practices, least-privilege access, appropriate logging, and secure data handling.
  • Design and maintain mappings and transformation pipelines for a transplant-focused OMOP CDM, representing transplant procedures, donor and recipient information, immunosuppressive therapies, laboratory results, rejection episodes, and longitudinal outcomes using appropriate standard concepts and documented extensions where needed.

Qualifications

  • Education: Master’s or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Computational Linguistics, Biomedical Informatics, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience: 7+ years of relevant experience in NLP, machine learning, or applied AI engineering, including 3+ years developing clinical NLP solutions using real-world EHR or hospital notes, with demonstrated delivery of production solutions.
  • Advanced Python and SQL skills, with experience using pandas or comparable data-processing tools, relational data modeling, ETL orchestration, incremental processing, schema validation, and automated data-quality checks.
  • Hands-on experience integrating structured EMR data through HL7 FHIR, HL7 v2, APIs, or database extracts; ability to align patient and encounter records, normalize units and timestamps, manage duplicates, and reconcile conflicting clinical sources.
  • Hands-on experience with the OMOP Common Data Model and OHDSI standardized vocabularies, including source-to-standard concept mapping, vocabulary relationships, and ETL development to transform structured EMR data and clinical NLP outputs into appropriate OMOP tables.
  • Experience validating OMOP data for conformance, completeness, and plausibility, with traceable source mappings and quality controls for longitudinal clinical records.
  • Hands-on experience with clinical entity recognition and linking, relationship extraction, assertion detection, and temporal extraction, including clinical sentence and section detection, abbreviation disambiguation, negation, uncertainty, and experiencer identification.
  • Experience implementing clinical NLP pipelines using medspaCy, scispaCy, cTAKES, or comparable frameworks, combining rules, dictionaries, and machine learning based on task requirements and measured performance.
  • Practical expertise with ICD, SNOMED CT, RxNorm, LOINC, and UMLS, including terminology services, value sets, semantic types, ontology hierarchies, concept retrieval and disambiguation, local-code crosswalks, and terminology version management; experience with unit normalization using UCUM or equivalent methods.
  • Experience applying and evaluating transformer models using PyTorch, TensorFlow, or equivalent frameworks and Hugging Face Transformers or comparable tooling; hands-on experience with LLM-based clinical extraction, schema-constrained outputs, and terminology-grounded validation.
  • Strong understanding of medical terminology, common diseases, laboratory measurements, medications, and clinical workflows. Ability to apply clinical reasoning to interpret documentation, distinguish evidence from inference, select appropriate concept specificity, and recognize ambiguous findings requiring clinician review.
  • Experience creating clinician-reviewed reference datasets and annotation guidelines; measuring precision, recall, and F1 for extraction, normalization, and assertion tasks; preventing patient-level data leakage; and evaluating performance across source systems and note types.
  • Experience building production APIs or services, deploying containerized applications on a cloud platform, and using Git, automated testing, CI/CD, model and data versioning, monitoring, batch inference, error recovery, and performance testing.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical work independently, mentor engineers, document designs and operational procedures, and communicate tradeoffs clearly to clinicians, clinical informaticists, scientists, data engineers, and business stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with transplant clinical data or research, including donor and recipient characteristics, immunosuppressive therapies, graft function, rejection, and longitudinal outcomes.
  • Experience with OHDSI tools such as Usagi, Achilles, or Data Quality Dashboard, and designing documented OMOP extensions when standard concepts or structures do not adequately represent domain requirements.
  • Experience adapting or fine-tuning biomedical or clinical language models, active learning, distributed processing, and optimizing inference for high-volume clinical data.
  • Experience with OCR and document layout processing for scanned clinical records, including assessment of how OCR errors affect extraction quality.

Additional Details:

Every individual at CareDx has a direct impact on our collective mission to improve the lives of organ transplant patients worldwide. We believe in taking great care of our people, so they take even greater care of our patients.

title: Research Intern, World Models and Synthetic Data for Autonomous Driving - Summer 2027
description:
Be part of the Autonomous Vehicle (AV) Applied Research team and help advance safe autonomy through generative world models and synthetic data. This internship is an opportunity to work alongside a team of researchers and engineers developing the next generation of models that can understand, simulate, and reason about complex driving environments.


We are looking for a passionate and highly motivated Research Intern with a strong background in machine learning and an interest in autonomous driving, generative world models, multimodal foundation models, and synthetic data generation. Our applied research team works closely with researchers and engineers across NVIDIA Research and the AV organization to develop scalable methods for training, evaluating, and improving autonomous systems.

Our research spans generative video and world models, controllable scenario generation, multimodal learning, end-to-end driving, 3D computer vision, and data-centric learning. We are particularly interested in using generative models to create diverse, safety-critical, and long-tail driving experiences that can help improve the robustness and generalization of autonomous systems.


As a Research Intern, you will contribute to research on generative data engines for autonomous driving: developing and using world models to understand data coverage, generate targeted driving scenarios, and study how synthetic data can systematically improve AV models. You will have the opportunity to develop new research ideas, run large-scale experiments, collaborate with experienced researchers and engineers, and contribute to publications at top-tier conferences.


What you'll be doing:

  • Research and prototype generative world models, traffic world models, and synthetic-data generation methods for autonomous driving.
  • Develop traffic world models that capture multi-agent interactions and realistic, reactive behaviors, enabling simulation and generation of complex driving scenarios.
  • Develop methods for controllable generation of diverse, interactive, and safety-critical driving scenarios.
  • Explore how generative video models, multimodal foundation models, traffic simulation, data curation, active learning, self-supervised learning, and simulation can improve training-data quality, diversity, and coverage.
  • Design and conduct experiments to understand how generated data affects AV model performance, robustness, and generalization.
  • Translate recent advances in generative modeling and machine learning into practical approaches for autonomous driving.
  • Collaborate closely with researchers and engineers across NVIDIA on research prototypes and experimental systems.
  • Contribute to high-impact research publications and open research efforts.

What we need to see:

  • Currently pursuing a Ph.D. or M.S. in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, Robotics, or a related field, with research experience in deep learning, computer vision, generative modeling, multimodal learning, robotics, or autonomous driving.
  • Strong foundations in machine learning and deep learning, with hands-on experience developing and evaluating neural-network models.
  • Experience in one or more of the following areas: generative models, video generation, multimodal learning, 3D computer vision, autonomous driving, or robotics.
  • Strong mathematical and analytical skills and an interest in designing rigorous experiments.
  • Strong Python programming skills and experience with modern deep learning frameworks.
  • Self-motivated, collaborative, and comfortable working in a research environment with open-ended problems.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Publications or research projects at conferences such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, or related venues.
  • Hands-on experience with generative world models, video generation, diffusion models, autoregressive models, multimodal foundation models, or synthetic-data generation.
  • Experience working with large-scale video, driving, robotics, or simulation datasets.
  • Experience with autonomous driving, embodied AI, physical AI, 3D scene understanding, or end-to-end learning.
  • Demonstrated ability to take a research idea from hypothesis → implementation → experimentation → quantitative evaluation.

title: Mexico AI Deployment Strategist
description:
About Telepatia

Telepatia AI is a healthtech company on a mission to transform healthcare in Latin America and beyond. Born at Stanford and built by doctors for doctors, our platform introduces AI Healthcare Employees that work invisibly inside clinical workflows: transcribing consultations in real time, generating structured medical records, offering evidence-based decision support, and integrating seamlessly with any current health system, all without disrupting the physician's flow.

Already adopted by thousands of doctors and leading hospitals across the region, Telepatia has demonstrated measurable impact: reducing cognitive load, improving patient experience, and increasing adherence to clinical protocols.

Our vision is bold: to turn scarcity into abundance by empowering healthcare professionals with scalable, trustworthy intelligence, and to pursue nothing less than the first Nobel Prize in Medicine for Latin America since 1984 with an AI Doctor.

About the role

A signed contract is where the real work starts. Every Mexican hospital, insurer or clinic chain we sign needs a deployment plan, clinical configuration that matches its specialties and protocols, physicians who adopt the product by choice, and a readout that proves the value the client was promised. The AI Deployment Strategist owns all of it.

You lead deployment for Telepatia in Mexico. You design the implementation playbook for the country, lead each site from kickoff to Ready for Use and adoption, manage the Onboarding Specialists on the ground, and sit with medical directors and operations leaders as their counterpart. You work hand in hand with the Country Manager, the global Medicine and Deployment teams, product and engineering.

Core skills: (i) Project leadership in complex healthcare organizations (ii) Clinical and operational judgment: what to configure, what to measure, what to push back on (iii) Change management with physicians and medical leadership.

One requirement: Be obsessed with adoption, not installation (and cool). Languages: Spanish (native), English (fluent).

What you will do

  • Design and run the deployment plan for every Mexican site: scope, specialties, timeline, success metrics, stakeholders and risks.

  • Lead clinical configuration with the Medicine team: note templates, protocols and alerts adapted to each institution and to Mexican guidelines (GPC, NOMs).

  • Hire, train and manage the Onboarding Specialists; set their weekly targets and coach them in the field.

  • Own pilot readouts: define the metrics with the client, track them weekly, and present results that convert pilots into contracts.

  • Run change management with medical directors, department heads and IT: training plans, communication, resistance handling.

  • Coordinate with Forward Deployed Engineers and the Integrations team on setup, EMR connections and technical issues.

  • Build the Mexico deployment playbook and feed field learnings back to product, engineering and the commercial team.

What we look for

More than experience, we look for attitude and drive.

  • 4 to 8 years in healthcare operations, hospital management, healthcare consulting or enterprise software implementation.

  • Track record leading complex, multi-stakeholder projects, ideally inside hospitals or health systems.

  • Comfort with data: you define metrics, build the readout and defend it to a medical director or CFO.

  • Executive presence with physicians and medical leadership; you earn trust fast.

  • Experience managing and developing a small team.

  • Willingness to travel to sites across Mexico.

Nice to have

  • Medical degree or clinical background (strongly preferred).

  • Experience deploying EMRs, clinical software or AI products in hospitals.

  • Knowledge of Mexican health regulation (NOM-004, NOM-024, LFPDPPP).

What we offer

  • Base salary: USD 3,000 to 6,000 per month, depending on experience.

  • Variable: tied to Ready for Use milestones and doctor adoption at the sites you own.

  • Equity participation.

  • Direct mentorship from the Country Manager and the global Deployment and Medicine teams.

  • Lead the deployment function in Mexico and grow the team under you.

  • Career progression into Head of Deployment Mexico or regional deployment leadership.

  • Immersion with the Deployment teams in Colombia and Brazil.

How we work

  • We're always on.

  • We own what we do and don't wait for anyone.

  • We move fast and with focus.

  • We play to win.

What this means for you

  • Ask questions. There are no silos; we grow by learning together.

  • Own your work. Don't wait until tomorrow; don't hand over unfinished work.

  • Speak up. Every voice matters, no matter the title.

  • Focus on impact. Prioritize what moves the needle.

  • Leave things better than you found them. Early stages are messy; your job is to make them less so.

Interview process

  1. Motivation and profile fit: 45 minutes with the People team.

  2. Deployment case: 60 minutes: plan the rollout of a named hospital and its pilot readout, with the Country Manager and the Deployment lead.

  3. Culture and values: 30 minutes with a founder.

title: Head of Product
description:
The Opportunity

Sharp Performance is hiring a Head of Product to own our product vision, strategy, and roadmap, and to build a product that first responders want to open every day. You will report to the CEO and work with Engineering, Design, Sales, Customer Success, and our coaching team to take product from founder-led to a disciplined, customer-driven function that balances consumer-grade craft with the realities of selling to agencies.

This is not a role you run from behind a dashboard. Our customers are cops and firefighters, and the person who wins here wants to be in the room with them: at the station, at the academy, on the ride-along, learning what they need by watching them use it. You are technical enough to go deep with engineering and earn their respect. You reason from the customer and the data, not from opinion. You have the backbone to tell the CEO no when the data says no, and the judgment to bring a better option when you do. You carry the craft of a great consumer product into a B2B world that rarely sees it.

How You'll Make an Impact

You own Sharp's product strategy end to end: what we build, why, and in what order. You hold a high bar for quality and experience and build a B2B product with the polish of the best consumer apps. When the tradeoffs are hard, you reason from the customer and the data, explain them clearly, and make a real recommendation, even when it is unpopular.

You stay close to the user. You sit with cops and firefighters, watch them use the product, and turn what you see into a clear, prioritized signal for what to build next. You define the outcomes and metrics that tell us whether the product is extending the service-life of the people who use it.

You partner across the company and build the team. You hold detailed technical conversations with engineering and weigh architecture and effort honestly. You align Sales, Customer Success, and coaching so the roadmap reflects what the market and our users need. You start hands-on as a player-coach, then hire, coach, and develop the product team as Sharp scales.

What You'll Need to Succeed

You have led the development of more than one product through real, high growth, not a single feature. You have built for business buyers and hold the craft bar of a great consumer product. Experience in public safety, govtech, digital health, or human performance is a strong plus, not a requirement.

You also bring:

  • Technical fluency: you can hold a detailed conversation with engineering and earn their respect
  • Customer obsession: time in the field with cops and firefighters energizes you rather than inconveniences you
  • Backbone: you tell the CEO no when the data says no, and you bring a better option
  • Range from strategy to hands-on execution in an early-stage, fast-moving company

Why You'll Want to Be Here

You will own the product function at a Series A company already working with 100+ public safety agencies, and your work helps improve the health, performance, and longevity of the people who run toward danger. Sharp is a small, fast-growing team, and our success starts with the people doing the work.

The package includes:

  • Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance for you and your family
  • Flexible PTO
  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity that reflect the seniority of the role
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Unlimited access to the Sharp Performance platform and our coaches

Sharp Performance is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace and encourage individuals of all backgrounds to apply. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

description:

The University offers a competitive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare and tuition benefits for employees and their families, generous retirement benefits, a wide variety of professional development opportunities, supportive work and family benefits, a wealth of health and wellness programs and resources, and much more.

**Posted Job Title**

Access and Disability Accommodations Specialist

**Job Profile Title**

Associate Director B, Academic Affairs, Community Engagement

**Job Description Summary**

Reporting to the Executive Director of Equal Opportunity (EO) in the University’s Center for Civil Rights (CCR), the Access and Disability Accommodations Specialist supports efforts to ensure compliance with the University’s Equal Opportunity and Nondiscrimination policies and guidelines, as well as federal, state, and local disability laws and regulations. The incumbent will respond to and facilitate the interactive process in response to reasonable accommodation requests from qualified staff, student-employees (including graduate workers), faculty, and campus visitors (except for applicants for admission and visiting families) and serve as a resource to the campus community on accessibility and disability inclusion, including through the development of policy and trainings to the Penn community.

**Job Description**

**Position Summary**

Reporting to the Executive Director of Equal Opportunity (EO) in the University’s Center for Civil Rights (CCR), the Access and Disability Accommodations Specialist supports efforts to ensure compliance with the University’s Equal Opportunity and Nondiscrimination policies and guidelines, as well as federal, state, and local disability laws and regulations. The incumbent will respond to and facilitate the interactive process in response to reasonable accommodation requests from qualified staff, student-employees (including graduate workers), faculty, and campus visitors (except for applicants for admission and visiting families) and serve as a resource to the campus community on accessibility and disability inclusion, including through the development of policy and trainings to the Penn community.

This role will also work in partnership with CCR’s Title IX and Religious and Ethnic Interests subject-matter experts to help determine whether reasonable accommodations and related services are appropriate for individuals served through those offices. This role will also actively collaborate with Student Disability Services (the Weingarten Center), Deans’ Offices, Human Resources (including Talent Acquisition), and other campus partners to support the provision of reasonable accommodations and related services. The Accommodations Specialist will support the University’s commitment to accessibility by promoting best practices and conducting outreach and educational initiatives in collaboration with other accessibility campus partners to increase awareness of accommodation obligations, accessibility, and accommodation resources across campus.

The Access and Disability Accommodations Specialist will play a key role in cultivating and supporting the University’s Center for Civil Rights. Serving as an essential point of contact within Equal Opportunity, this position will engage with qualified staff, student-employees, faculty, and campus visitors seeking reasonable accommodations, and advance equitable access to University programs, services, and opportunities. This role will provide guidance throughout the accommodation process and help advance the University’s commitment to civil rights compliance and equal access for all members of the campus community and may also be asked to provide support for other activities within the CCR.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

- Build trusting partnerships with qualified staff, student-employees (including graduate workers), faculty, and campus visitors with disabilities and provide individualized support, guidance, and resources to help them thrive in the workplace.
- Serve as a primary point of contact for qualified staff, student employees (including graduate workers), faculty, and campus visitors requesting reasonable accommodations based on disability.
- Facilitate the individualized, interactive process in response to each reasonable accommodation request, including through conducting intake and follow-up meetings, consulting with supervisors and/or other campus leadership, as appropriate, reviewing supporting documentation, and making a written accommodation determination in response to the request.
- Work with campus partners on the implementation of approved reasonable accommodations.
- For student employees (including graduate workers), collaborate with colleagues in the Center for Civil Rights and Student Disability Services (the Weingarten Center) as appropriate to respond to and facilitate the interactive process in response to student-employee accommodation requests, including to provide consistent support and implementation, and to develop an understanding of the external resources available to support individuals with accommodation requests.
- Document incoming accommodation requests and consultations as well as the interactive process, including the initial request, intake, activities and steps taken in response, outcome, and the implementation of accommodations, as appropriate.
- Ensure accommodation request files reflect the request, the university’s response, and information relied upon to make an accommodation determination, and document the request and response timeline, reflecting prompt institutional responses and/or any documented reasons for delay.
- Assist with the administration and maintenance of the accommodation database, ensuring accurate and timely recordkeeping, while promoting best practices in data management, privacy, accessibility, and accommodation processes.
- Connect staff, student-employees (including graduate workers), faculty, and campus visitors with University accessibility-related resources and promote equitable access to University programs and services by collaborating with University campus and community organizations.
- Serve as a resource on disability and accessibility for staff, student‑employees (including graduate workers), faculty, and campus visitors and the broader University community by providing guidance, consultation, and support on accommodation processes and accessibility considerations, and by conducting education and training on accessibility and disability inclusion.
- Participate in the review and revision of the Equal Opportunity’s accessibility-related policies and procedures to reflect current federal, state and local legal standards and best practices, including under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act, and the Fair Housing Act.
- Serve on committees and working groups supporting initiatives and compliance with the University’s Equal Opportunity and Nondiscrimination policies and guidelines by contributing subject‑matter expertise and partnership across University efforts.
- Maintain current knowledge of regulatory requirements and best practices related to accessibility and disability inclusion and monitor developments in relevant laws, regulations, guidelines, and professional standards, including under the ADA and the Rehabilitation Act.
- Develop working knowledge of, and competency with, available assistive technology, adaptive equipment, auxiliary aids and services, alternative formats, learning enhancement tools, and general digital accessibility (WCAG 2.1)
- Perform other duties as assigned, which may include supporting additional EO or CCR activities and initiatives as needed.

**Essential Characteristics**

- Knowledge of disability inclusion, accessibility, and relevant federal, state and local laws, including the ADA, the Rehabilitation Act, Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, Philadelphia Fair Practices Ordinance, FERPA and the FHA.
- Ability to facilitate the interactive process through the engagement with the requestor as well as relevant campus partners, as appropriate, to determine potential appropriate reasonable accommodations.
- Strong case‑management, organization, collaboration, and communication skills.
- Experience in a higher education environment, including in working with and across higher education student, faculty, and staff stakeholders and leadership.
- Exceptional attention to detail.
- Ability to work collaboratively across departments and handle sensitive, confidential information.
- Ability to maintain records and manage databases.
- Experience developing and delivering training programs.
- Commitment to creating an equitable and accessible environment.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Sound judgement, discretion, and cultural competence.

**Required Qualifications**

- A bachelor’s degree and 2-3 years of experience in appropriate area or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Candidates with a Juris Doctor (JD) degree will also be considered.
- Experience in disability services, human resources, equal employment opportunity, employee relations, accommodations management, or a related field.

Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

Human Resources

$58,506.00 - $75,000.00 Annual Rate

title: Production Worker
description:
Assembly Line Production Worker

Build Quality. Work as a Team. Keep Production Moving.

Procore International is looking for a reliable and hands-on Assembly Line Production Worker to join our manufacturing team.

If you enjoy working with your hands, using tools, and seeing the results of your work at the end of the day, this could be a great opportunity to build your experience in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

What You’ll Be Doing

As part of our production team, you’ll help assemble radiator components and related products while ensuring quality, safety, and production standards are met.

You will:

  • Assemble radiator components and pre-manufactured parts using hand and power tools
  • Fasten, align, and secure components according to work instructions, drawings, and specifications
  • Install radiators and related replacement components
  • Perform basic testing and visual inspections to identify defects or assembly issues
  • Complete soldering and other assembly-related tasks
  • Clean, prepare, stage, and handle materials throughout the production process
  • Support inventory counts and material handling as needed
  • Keep your work area clean, organized, and safe
  • Work with your team to meet daily production targets and delivery schedules

What We’re Looking For

You don’t need to know everything on day one. We’re looking for someone who is reliable, mechanically inclined, comfortable working with their hands, and willing to learn.

Ideally, you bring:

  • Basic mechanical aptitude or familiarity with automotive or mechanical components
  • Comfort using hand and power tools
  • Good attention to detail
  • Ability to follow instructions and established processes
  • A strong focus on quality and safety
  • Reliability and consistent attendance
  • Ability to work well as part of a production team
  • Willingness to learn new tools, equipment, and processes

What to Expect

This is a hands-on role in a manufacturing and assembly environment. You’ll be standing and moving throughout your shift and completing repetitive assembly tasks. The work may involve bending, reaching, lifting, carrying, pushing, and pulling moderate weights.

You’ll also work around typical manufacturing noise and equipment and will be required to wear appropriate PPE, including safety footwear, gloves, and eye protection.

Why This Role?

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys hands-on mechanical work and wants to develop their skills in manufacturing. Whether you already have production experience or are looking to build it, we’re looking for people who show up, work safely, take pride in quality, and contribute to the team.

Interested in joining Procore International? Apply today.
